author: chronark
body:
## Summary

  Fix flaky CI caused by `libopenapi-validator`'s unsafe concurrent schema rendering.

  ## The problem

  Concurrent tests (`TestSetRolesConcurrent`, `TestSetPermissionsConcurrent`, `TestAddPermissionsConcurrent`, etc.) intermittently failed with:

  `schema render failure, circular reference detected during inline rendering`

  ## Root cause

  `libopenapi-validator` shares a mutable document model across all calls to `ValidateHttpRequest`. When the
  validator's internal **schema cache** is cold (first request for a given endpoint), it calls
  `RenderInlineWithContext` to render and compile the schema. If multiple goroutines hit a cold cache
  simultaneously, they all try to render the same schema concurrently, corrupting the shared document state.

  The upstream library attempted to fix this in
  [pb33f/libopenapi#488](https://github.com/pb33f/libopenapi/pull/488) by adding per-call `InlineRenderContext` for
   cycle tracking, but the underlying document model remains unsafe for concurrent rendering.

  ## What we tried and learned

  | Approach | Result |
  |----------|--------|
  | **Retry loop (1–10 attempts)** | ~1–6 failures per 10k requests regardless of retry count. Retrying doesn't help because the corrupted state persists — it's not transient. |
  | **`ValidateHttpRequestSync`** | Same failure rate. The race isn't in the validator's internal goroutines, it's in the shared document model between concurrent callers. |
  | **Mutex** | 0/100k failures. Works, but serializes all validation. |
  | **Schema cache warm-up** | 0/100k failures. A single request per endpoint before concurrent traffic populates the cache. Subsequent requests skip rendering entirely. |

  ## The fix
  1. **Switched to `ValidateHttpRequestSync`** — avoids unnecessary internal goroutines in the validator.
  2. **Added a warm-up request** before each concurrent test so the schema cache is populated before the burst.


  ## Note

  This is a workaround. The real fix is moving off `libopenapi-validator`, which is planned. The warm-up pattern
  only protects tests — in production the first concurrent requests to a cold validator could still race, though
  the probability is very low (~1 in 10k) and only affects the very first request after a deploy.

author: sordina
body:
# Exploring Spike-Clojure Ideas

**Branch:** lyndon/exploring-spike-lisp-ideas
**Date:** 2026-03-26

## Context

Spike-Clojure is a round-trippable text representation of the graph — a true Clojure subset where graph semantics layer on top of ordinary Clojure code without breaking host-language validity. It serves as the backing format for the text view (§6.5) and the AI/MCP interface (§13).

This branch designed the notation and built the base reader. The semantic interpreter and serialiser are deferred.

## Approach

- [x] **1. Understand the gap** — resolved as a design question (see decisions below); no separate document needed.
- [x] **2. Base-lisp reader** (`src/graph/base_lisp.ts`) — EDN-inspired S-expression reader; typed `SExp` AST, no graph semantics.
- [x] **3. Candidate syntax stories** (`src/ui/stories/candidate-spike-lisp-syntaxes.stories.tsx`) — 13 stories covering all syntax patterns: structural containers, call topology, ports, fan-out/fan-in/diamond, URI references, properties.
- [ ] **4. Semantic interpreter + serialiser** (`src/graph/spike_lisp.ts`) — deferred; needs targeting at `def`/`defn`/`fn` semantics (not the original `#Subgraph`/`#Call` approach). See Deferred.
- [ ] **5. Round-trip tests** (`src/graph/spike_lisp_test.ts`) — deferred; depends on interpreter.
- [x] **6. Bridge exploration** — resolved as a design question; no converter file needed. See decisions below.
- [x] **7. Update DESIGN.md** — §13.2 replaced with language-representation model; `docs/spike-clojure.md` created with full Spike-Clojure reference. §5.3 updated with sketch/enforce modes and UI layer relationship.

## Resolved Decisions

- **Rename: Spike-Lisp → Spike-Clojure** — the Clojure variant is a true Clojure subset. Future variants (TypeScript, Scheme, etc.) will have their own names. The base reader layer remains "base-lisp" (language-agnostic).

- **Isomorphism with idiomatic code** — the goal is not merely Clojure-inspired syntax but full isomorphism: valid Spike-Clojure is valid Clojure. When a design choice arises, prefer the idiomatic host-language form. Non-host forms (`#Subgraph`, `#Call`) are reserved for concepts with no natural host-language equivalent.

- **Core forms: `def` / `defn` / `fn`**
  - `def` — structural container, named value, not callable; body is a vector of node references: `(def my-graph [A B C])`
  - `defn` — callable node, has ports, can be invoked; body is a plain `let` returning a map
  - `fn` — anonymous sub-subgraph

- **`def` body is a vector of bare symbol references** — `(node)` invocation syntax inside a structural container incorrectly implied calling the node. Bare refs express presence without call order.

- **Inline named `def` inside a vector** — `(def A [B (def C [D])])` is valid shorthand, equivalent to separate `(def C [D])` + `(def A [B C])`. Use separate forms when the sub-container is shared or deeply nested.

- **`#Subgraph` and `#Call` are optional annotations** — `def`/`defn`/`fn` already carry the structural/callable distinction. `#Subgraph`/`#Call` are retained as optional explicit annotations and as the extensibility hook for user-defined semantic variants.

- **Port syntax** — in-ports are `defn` arguments with `^Type` hints; out-ports use the attr-map position:
  - Single output: `(defn ^float foo [^float x] ...)` — standard Clojure type hint
  - Multiple outputs: `(defn foo {:ports {:x1 float :x2 float}} [^float a] ...)` — attr-map, same position as `:deprecated`, `:arglists` etc.

- **Port selection via Clojure destructuring** — `(let [{:keys [port-name]} (node args)] ...)` replaces the Spike-Lisp-specific `:from :port-name`. Standard Clojure, no graph-specific syntax.

- **Node identity in call graphs via `let`** — implicit label deduplication (D appearing twice = same node) is fragile. `let` binding is the resolution: `(let [d D] (A (B d) (C d)))` — `d` is a named reference shared across branches. Also handles pure fan-in and named-wire semantics.

- **UI layer vs. formal types** — the UI type system (`TreeNode`/`Edge`) is intentionally permissive. It can author all graph concepts (ports, schemas, implementations) but does not structurally require any of them — fields are optional, not absent. There is no separate "formal type" the UI must be converted into; the UI is the authoring model. The constraint system provides enforcement:
  - **sketch mode** — constraints surface feedback but do not block
  - **enforce mode** — violations are hard stops at declared checkpoints (save, compile, publish)
  - Relationship: **enforce-valid ⊆ sketch-valid ⊆ UI-representable**

## Deferred

Items to revisit in a future branch:

- **Semantic interpreter** (`src/graph/spike_lisp.ts`) — implement `interpret(sexp: SExp): Graph` targeting the `def`/`defn`/`fn` semantics. The original plan targeted `#Subgraph`/`#Call`; needs re-scoping.
- **Serialiser** (`src/graph/spike_lisp.ts`) — implement `serialize(graph: Graph): string`; emit `def`/`defn`/`fn` forms. Inline subgraph by default; fall back to URI reference.
- **Round-trip tests** (`src/graph/spike_lisp_test.ts`) — depends on interpreter + serialiser.
- **ID/URI tagging for `defn` forms** — how does a `defn` declare its own URI? Open: `{:uri "spike://..."}` in the attr-map, or a separate `defn` metadata convention.
- **`defn` body as bare `#Subgraph`** — if the body is a `#Subgraph` rather than a `let`, does that mean the node's implementation *is* the containment graph, or that the node *is* the graph? Needs pinning down.
- **User-defined semantic variants** — extensibility model for `#MyVariant` reader tags beyond `#Subgraph`/`#Call`.
- **Spike-TypeScript, Spike-Scheme variants** — future language variants following the same isomorphism principle. Base-lisp reader is shared; only the semantic mapping layer differs.
- **Inout ports** — bidirectional ports. Call-graph invocation already handles request/response implicitly; explicit inout ports deferred.
- **Correlated input/output types** — e.g. `(defn id [^T x] ^T)` where output type mirrors input. Requires type-level polymorphism / dynamic dispatch. Out of scope for now.
- **Two-finger pan, pinch-to-zoom** — replace drag-to-zoom with trackpad gestures.
- **Data explorer modal** — larger rendering of data/type information for nodes and edges.

## Critical Files

- `src/graph/base_lisp.ts` — base-lisp reader (done)
- `src/ui/stories/candidate-spike-lisp-syntaxes.stories.tsx` — syntax candidate stories (done)
- `docs/spike-clojure.md` — Spike-Clojure reference documentation (done)
- `DESIGN.md` §5.3 — sketch/enforce modes, UI layer relationship (done)
- `DESIGN.md` §13.2 — language representation model (done)
- `src/graph/spike_lisp.ts` — semantic interpreter + serialiser (deferred)
- `src/graph/spike_lisp_test.ts` — round-trip tests (deferred)

## Diversions

- **2026-03-28 — CI `deno task ci`** — lint error (`no-unused-vars` on `_open` param). Fixed. Added `ci` task to `deno.json`; updated `CLAUDE.md` to require it before every commit.
- **2026-03-29 — CI `check-ui` missing** — `TS2503: Cannot find namespace 'JSX'`. Fixed import; added `check-ui` to the `ci` task.

## Verification

- [x] `NO_COLOR=1 deno task ci` passes (fmt, lint, type-check, tests)
- [x] Syntax stories cover all syntax patterns (13 stories)
- [x] DESIGN.md updated with language-representation model and sketch/enforce modes
- [x] `docs/spike-clojure.md` created with full reference
- [ ] Round-trip: `interpret(parse(serialize(fixture)))` deep-equals fixture — deferred
- [ ] Semantic interpreter covers `def`/`defn`/`fn` forms — deferred

body:
## Overview
This PR delivers the complete, production-ready **Lingo.dev Go SDK**. It achieves full feature parity with the existing Python, JavaScript, and PHP SDKs (excluding HTML processing, which remains JS-only). 

The SDK has been built from the ground up to follow Go best practices, featuring robust concurrency, context propagation, comprehensive error handling, and fully automated CI/CD pipelines.

Closes https://github.com/lingodotdev/lingo.dev/issues/1073

## 🚀 What's Included

### Core SDK Features
- **Full API Surface:** Implemented `LocalizeText`, `LocalizeObject`, `LocalizeChat`, `BatchLocalizeText`, `BatchLocalizeObjects`, `RecognizeLocale`, and `WhoAmI`.
- **First-Class Context Support:** Every method accepts `context.Context` as the first parameter, propagating all the way down to `http.NewRequestWithContext` for reliable request cancellation.
- **Resilience:** Automatic exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s) on 5xx server errors and network failures (4xx errors fail fast).
- **Concurrent Chunk Processing:** Large payloads are automatically split into chunks and processed in parallel using `golang.org/x/sync/errgroup`.
- **Typed Error Handling:** Introduced `ValueError` for validation/400 errors and `RuntimeError` (with a `StatusCode` field) for server/network errors.
- **Flexible Configuration:** Utilizes functional options (`SetURL`, `SetBatchSize`, `SetIdealBatchItemSize`) for clean client initialization.

### 🧪 Testing (82.6% Coverage)
- **Unit Tests (30 tests):** Comprehensive testing using `httptest.NewServer` covering config validation, chunking, truncation, error types, and core endpoints.
- **Integration Tests (9 tests):** Real API verification against production endpoints. (Automatically skipped when `LINGODOTDEV_API_KEY` is not set).
- **Mocked Integration Tests (7 tests):** Validates complex internal logic including retry behavior, concurrent parallelism, context cancellation, and workflow ID consistency.
- **Performance:** Unit + Mocked tests complete in ~13s; Full integration suite completes in ~60s.

### ⚙️ CI/CD & Automation
- **PR Workflow:** Matrix testing across Go 1.21 and 1.22. Includes build, `vet`, `gofmt` checks, conditional integration tests, and coverage uploads to Codecov.
- **Release Workflow:** Automated semantic versioning driven by conventional commits, automated changelog generation via `git-chglog`, and GitHub release creation.
- **Standards:** Added a PR template enforcing conventional commit guidelines.

### 📚 Documentation
- **Comprehensive README:** Includes CI badges, runnable examples for every method, a configuration table, full API references, and sections on error handling and Go-specific advantages.
- **Developer Experience:** Added a fully runnable `examples/main.go` and a `Makefile` with targets for `test`, `test-integration`, `test-coverage`, `build`, `vet`, `fmt`, `lint`, and `clean`.

## 🏗️ Architecture & Request Flow

```text
Client.LocalizeText(ctx, ...)
  → localizeRaw(ctx, ...)
    → ExtractChunks(payload)
    → localizeChunk(ctx, ...) [sequential or concurrent via errgroup]
      → do(ctx, ...) [retries, JSON parsing, returns full response]
        → http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, ...)
 ```
 ## 📝 Technical Notes for Reviewers
- **Context Flow:** Canceling the provided context will successfully abort in-flight HTTP requests natively. *(Note: Retry logic sleeps between attempts but does not currently check context during the sleep timer).*
- **Unified HTTP Layer:** The internal `do()` method returns a `map[string]any` representing the full JSON response. This allows divergent response structures (like `/recognize` vs `/i18n`) to pass through the same robust HTTP and retry layer. Callers extract exactly what they need.
- **Concurrency:** Batch methods rely on `errgroup.WithContext` to manage parallel execution, ensuring automatic cancellation of sibling routines if one fails.

## 📦 Dependencies
- `golang.org/x/sync` — Utilized `errgroup` for safe concurrent chunk and batch processing.
- `github.com/matoous/go-nanoid/v2` — Used for robust workflow ID generation.

### Motivation
- Entry decision logic was scattered across `decision`, `timing`, `stage`, and sizing, causing inconsistent UI/Promote behavior and duplicated gating logic.

- Added helper `classify_entry_status(...)` that derives a runtime `entry_state` (`READY` / `WAIT` / `NO_ENTRY`) from `decision`, `timing`, `liquidity health`, `anti_rug`, and `size_info` and returns reasons, rank and `can_promote` flags.

body:
## Summary
- Handle backend error events (`payload.error`) in SSE stream parser instead of silently ignoring them
- Refine `classifyError` to only flag real network TypeErrors (`Failed to fetch`, `NetworkError`, `Load failed`) instead of all `TypeError`s
- Add dedicated classification for backend errors forwarded via SSE with sub-classification (timeout/server)
- Improve user-facing error messages for clarity

## Context
The "Problème de connexion réseau" error was showing too frequently because:
1. All `TypeError` exceptions were classified as network errors, but `TypeError` in JS can occur for many non-network reasons (accessing undefined properties, parsing failures, etc.)
2. Backend SSE error events (`{"error": true, "message": "..."}`) were silently ignored by the frontend parser, causing downstream TypeErrors that were then misclassified as network issues

## Changes
**`chatbot.blade.php`**:
- Added `payload.error` handling in the SSE event loop (before `payload.final_response` check) - throws a properly flagged `Error` with `isBackendError = true`
- Rewrote `classifyError()`:
  - Backend errors (`isBackendError`) are sub-classified into timeout/server based on the actual backend message
  - Network errors now only match real fetch failures (`Failed to fetch`, `NetworkError`, `Load failed`, `fetch failed`, `ERR_NETWORK`, `ERR_CONNECTION`)
  - Improved all user-facing messages

author: behnam-deriv
body:
# fix: reduce CPU usage on line chart area fill during Y-axis zoom

## Problem

High CPU usage was observed on the line chart when the Y-axis was zoomed in (vertical padding at minimum). The effect was noticeably worse the more zoomed in the chart was, and improved significantly when zoomed out to maximum padding.

### Root cause

The investigation traced the bottleneck to `canvas.drawPath` in `LinePainter.onPaintData`, specifically the area fill drawn beneath the line series.

The area fill path is closed all the way down to the bottom of the canvas (`size.height`). This means the filled polygon covers a pixel area proportional to how much vertical space the line occupies:

- **Zoomed in (min padding):** the line spreads across most of the canvas height → the filled polygon covers nearly the entire canvas → maximum GPU fill work.
- **Zoomed out (max padding):** the line is compressed into a small band near the centre → the filled polygon covers very few pixels → minimal GPU fill work.

`canvas.drawPath` with `PaintingStyle.fill` must rasterise every pixel inside the polygon. The cost scales directly with the number of pixels covered, so CPU usage rose and fell with the zoom level.

Anti-aliasing compounded the cost. Flutter's rasteriser computes sub-pixel edge coverage for every boundary pixel of the filled polygon. For a large filled shape spanning hundreds of pixels vertically this is significant overhead.

The area fill edges are not visible to the user — they sit directly beneath the stroked line drawn on top — so anti-aliased edges on the fill provide no visual benefit.

## Solution

Disabling anti-aliasing on the area fill paint:

```dart
final Paint areaPaint = Paint()
  ..style = PaintingStyle.fill
  ..isAntiAlias = false   // added
  ..shader = ui.Gradient.linear(...);
```

Setting `isAntiAlias = false` tells the rasteriser to skip sub-pixel edge computation entirely and fill pixels with a hard cutoff. Since the stroke line already covers the fill boundary, the visual result is identical to the user while the per-frame GPU cost is substantially reduced regardless of zoom level.

author: rodrigovalecred
body:
### 💡 What:
Adicionado `.cache()` ao DataFrame `df_daily_agg` no notebook `NB_Gold_Carteira_Valor_Diario.Notebook` logo após sua criação (que envolve um dispendioso `explode` e `groupBy`), e chamado `df_daily_agg.unpersist()` ao final da execução do script para liberar memória.

### 🎯 Why:
O DataFrame `df_daily_agg` é utilizado em três ações distintas subsequentes:
1. `df_daily_agg.write.saveAsTable()`
2. `df_daily_agg.select(count, max).collect()` (Dashboard)
3. `df_daily_agg.filter().agg().collect()` (Dashboard)

Sem o `.cache()`, o otimizador Catalyst do PySpark reavalia a linhagem inteira (Logical Plan) e reexecuta as etapas pesadas de "FileScan" seguidas por "Generate" (explosão do array de datas) e shuffle (`groupBy`) três vezes distintas para cada uma dessas ações. Isso cria lentidão extrema, desperdício de I/O em leitura, e uso desnecessário de CPU do cluster.

### 📊 Impacto:
Reduz em até 66% o processamento do pipeline lógico, limitando a execução do `explode` de datas a uma única vez por lote. Diminui significativamente o tempo de geração do dashboard da Carteira Diária, eliminando gargalos de I/O.

### 🔬 Measurement:
A visualização do Spark UI ou a função `df_daily_agg.explain()` exibirá que para as ações de coleta (`collect`) posteriores, o plano físico acionará o uso de um `InMemoryTableScan`, ao invés de reiniciar pelo `FileScan` seguido pela operação `Generate` massiva.

author: synteracloud
body:
### Motivation

- Provide a production baseline for audit logging, request tracing, and basic observability to satisfy B1-P06::AUDIT_OBSERVABILITY requirements (audit logs, request tracing, observability hooks). 
- Close blind spots by defining immutable audit events and enforcement rules so all critical actions are captured and queryable by compliance tooling.

### Description

- Added a new spec at `docs/observability-audit.md` defining a structured logging contract, severity/retention rules, field redaction requirements, and mandatory security event categories. 
- Added request tracing guidance using W3C Trace Context, required spans for mutating flows, span attributes, and a sampling strategy. 
- Defined basic observability hooks including metrics, health endpoints, alert triggers, and Prometheus/OpenTelemetry integration notes. 
- Defined an immutable audit event schema and audit APIs (`GET /v1/audit/events`, `GET /v1/audit/events/{event_id}`, `POST /v1/audit/exports`, `GET /v1/audit/exports/{job_id}`, and `GET /v1/audit/integrity/verify`) with authorization requirements. 
- Added a critical-action coverage matrix and enforcement controls (CI check + runtime fallback `audit.mapping.missing`) and an implementation plan including `AuditWriter.append(event)` and middleware for `request_id`/`trace_id`/tenant binding. 
- Updated `docs/security-model.md` to reference the new implementation baseline (`docs/observability-audit.md`).

# Before

    username: ${{ github.actor }}
    password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

author: mmaghsoodnia
body:
## Summary

- Adds a new `docs format` subcommand for applying rich text formatting to existing text in Google Docs
- Adds formatting flags (`--font-family`, `--font-size`, `--text-color`, `--bg-color`, `--bold`, `--italic`, `--underline`, `--strikethrough`, `--alignment`, `--line-spacing`) to `docs write`
- Uses Google Docs API `batchUpdate` with `UpdateTextStyle` and `UpdateParagraphStyle` requests

### `docs format` command

Target text by content match or apply to entire document:

```bash
# Format specific text
gog docs format <docId> --match "Hello World" --bold --text-color "#FF0000"

# Format all occurrences
gog docs format <docId> --match "important" --match-all --underline --bg-color "#FFFF00"

# Format entire document
gog docs format <docId> --font-family "Georgia" --font-size 14
```

### `docs write` formatting

Apply formatting after writing content:

```bash
gog docs write <docId> --text "Hello" --font-family "Arial" --font-size 16 --text-color "#003399"
```

### Implementation

- `FormattingOpts` struct + `buildFormattingRequests()` in `docs_formatter.go` — builds typed API requests with proper field masks
- `DocsFormatCmd` in `docs_edit.go` — reuses existing `findTextInDoc`/`findTextMatches` for text search
- Reuses existing `parseHexColor` from `docs_sed_helpers.go` via `hexToOptionalColor` wrapper
- Supports `ForceSendFields` for explicitly setting boolean values to `false` (e.g., removing bold)

## Test plan

- [ ] `gog docs format <id> --match "text" --bold --text-color "#FF0000"` — verify bold red text in browser
- [ ] `gog docs format <id> --match "text" --match-all --underline` — verify all occurrences underlined
- [ ] `gog docs format <id> --alignment center` — verify whole doc centered
- [ ] `gog docs write <id> --text "Hello" --font-family Georgia --font-size 16` — verify font applied
- [ ] `gog docs format <id> --match "nonexistent"` — verify error message

author: tcutts
body:
### Fix unsafe shell variable expansions and quoting in launcher scripts

All launcher scripts (aprun_launch.sh, jsrun_launch.sh, mpi_launch.sh, multi_launch.sh, single_launch.sh, srun_launch.sh) and the test launcher.sh had several quoting issues that would cause failures when paths contain spaces. This PR fixes them all:

1. Replaced source $(dirname "$0")/launcher_lib.sh with source "${0%/*}/launcher_lib.sh" in all scripts, using shell parameter expansion to avoid both the unquoted command substitution and the nested quoting problem that would result from quoting it.
2. Quoted all uses of $_PSI_J_STDOUT, $_PSI_J_STDERR, $_PSI_J_STDIN, $_PSI_J_PROCESS_COUNT, and $_PSI_J_EC in redirections and command arguments throughout all scripts.

In launcher_lib.sh:

1. Added a _psi_j_abspath() helper that resolves all incoming path arguments to absolute paths at startup, preventing misresolution if the working directory changes during execution.
2. Replaced backtick command substitution in ts() with $(...).
3. On bash 4.2+, ts() now uses printf '%(%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S)T' — a zero-fork builtin — instead of spawning a date subprocess for every line of output. The original date-based implementation is retained as a fallback for older bash.

For 10,000 lines of output this saves about 18 seconds of execution time (benchmarked on an M1 Macbook)

## Summary
- Fixes the non-streaming (finite) RX path in the xlnx AXI DMA SG driver
- `dma_config()` was dividing total transfer size by `num_bds` (1024), creating tiny BDs misaligned with FPGA TLAST boundaries
- Adds `active_bds` field and `dest_scatter_count` support for caller-specified per-burst BD sizing
- Handles mode transitions (streaming <-> finite) with proper soft reset and state cleanup

## Changes
- `active_bds` field tracks how many BDs are used in finite transfers (0 = all)
- `build_bd_ring`: builds only `active_bds` entries for finite RX
- `kick_channel`: TAILDESC set to `active_bds - 1` for finite RX
- RX ISR: scans completed BDs and computes `last_rx_bytes` for non-streaming path
- `dma_config`: forces soft reset if RX channel not halted (stale streaming state)
- `reconfigure_rx`: unconditional soft reset + clears `active_bds`/`error` before rebuilding ring

body:
### Motivation
- Provide deterministic, repeatable experiment scenarios and a way to apply them to the runtime for safety validation and audits.
- Allow automated runtime repositioning in PX4 simulator and deterministic user-position shaping to validate planner/safety behavior across modes.
- Capture detailed task run telemetry and events into a spreadsheet to support experiment analysis and debugging.
- Expose scenario selection, preview, apply and 4-mode audit in the Web UI for operator-driven tests.

### Description
- Add `controller/experiment_scenarios.py` that defines frozen `ExperimentScenario` entries and `normalize_scenario_name` for deterministic modes (`SAFE`, `CAUTION`, `WARNING`, `DANGER`).
- Introduce `controller/scenario_manager.py` to project scenario safety, apply scenarios to a running `LLMController`, perform runtime calibration of user offsets, and produce `ScenarioApplyReport` results.
- Add `controller/task_run_logger.py` which logs run-level and event-level telemetry to an Excel workbook using `openpyxl` when available, and exposes `start_run`, `update_plan_info`, `consume_runtime_snapshot`, and `end_run` APIs.
- Integrate scenario and logging features into `controller/llm_controller.py` by adding `ScenarioManager` and `TaskRunLogger` instances, starting/stopping a monitor thread during `execute_task_description`, recording plan/execution outcomes, and exposing scenario-related helper methods (`set_active_scenario`, `apply_selected_scenario`, `get_scenario_projection`, `get_scenario_runtime_status`, `get_initial_scenario_state`).
- Add `reposition_for_scenario` to `controller/px4_sim_robot_wrapper.py` to reposition the simulated vehicle and set yaw, with retries and tolerance adjustments.
- Extend `controller/sim_state_provider.py` to support `set_user_position`, `lock_user_position`, and to ignore incoming user position updates while locked, plus internal tracking for the locked reason.
- Tweak fuzzy safety membership rule constants in `controller/fuzzy_safety_assessor.py` to adjust numeric mapping of gap/uncertainty combinations.
- Wire UI controls in `serving/webui/typefly.py` to present a scenario dropdown, preview/apply buttons and a 4-mode audit action, and to surface initial scenario state in the coordinates/safety panels.
- Add `openpyxl` to `serving/webui/install_requirements.sh` so `TaskRunLogger` can persist run sheets.

### Testing

author: binhnt92
body:
## Summary

Fixes an unbounded memory leak in the gateway's agent caching system. Expired sessions leave their AIAgent instances permanently in `_agent_cache`, and the cache has no size limit.

## Problem

The gateway caches `AIAgent` instances per session to preserve Anthropic prompt caching across turns (`_agent_cache` dict at `gateway/run.py:357`). When a session expires, `_session_expiry_watcher` (line 1126) flushes memories and shuts down Honcho — but never calls `_evict_cached_agent()`. Each leaked agent holds an API client, system prompt, full message history, memory store, Honcho manager, todo store, and image fallback cache.

Additionally, `_agent_cache` is a plain `Dict` with no maximum size and no TTL. Every unique session creates a permanent entry until process restart. On a public-facing gateway running for days/weeks, this grows without bound.

## Fixes

**1. Evict on session expiry** (`gateway/run.py`)

Added `self._evict_cached_agent(key)` call in `_session_expiry_watcher` right after `_shutdown_gateway_honcho(key)`, matching the pattern already used by `/new` and `/reset` handlers (line 2704).

**2. LRU size cap** (`gateway/run.py`)

When storing a new agent in the cache, evict the oldest entry if the cache exceeds 200 entries. Provides a hard upper bound on memory growth even if the expiry watcher misses sessions.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `gateway/run.py` | Add `_evict_cached_agent(key)` in expiry watcher; add 200-entry LRU eviction on cache store |
| `tests/gateway/test_agent_cache_eviction.py` | 3 new tests: eviction removes entry, nonexistent key is no-op, size cap enforced |

author: kibanamachine
body:
# Backport

This will backport the following commits from `main` to `9.3`:
 - [Handle unavailable_shards_exception as retryable in SO v2 migrations (#257775)](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/257775)

<!--- Backport version: 9.6.6 -->

### Questions ?
Please refer to the [Backport tool documentation](https://github.com/sorenlouv/backport)

<!--BACKPORT [{"author":{"name":"Rudolf Meijering","email":"skaapgif@gmail.com"},"sourceCommit":{"committedDate":"2026-03-19T14:56:33Z","message":"Handle unavailable_shards_exception as retryable in SO v2 migrations (#257775)

## Summary

- SO v2 migrations fail fatally when `bulkOverwriteTransformedDocuments`
encounters `unavailable_shards_exception` (e.g. when not all shard
copies are active during bulk writes with `wait_for_active_shards:
'all'`)
- This PR recognizes `unavailable_shards_exception` as a retryable error
and retries indefinitely with exponential backoff (matching the
`wait_for_task_completion_timeout` precedent using
`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`)
- Affects both `REINDEX_SOURCE_TO_TEMP_INDEX_BULK` and
`TRANSFORMED_DOCUMENTS_BULK_INDEX` migration states
- Also handles the error in the ZDT model since
`bulkOverwriteTransformedDocuments` is shared

### Error before this fix
```
[.kibana_security_solution] Reason: Unable to complete saved object migrations for the [.kibana_security_solution] index.
Error: [{"type":"unavailable_shards_exception","reason":"[.kibana_security_solution_9.0.1_001][0] Not enough active copies to meet shard count of [ALL] (have 1, needed 2). Timeout: [1m], request: [BulkShardRequest [...] containing [1000] requests]"}]
```

### Changes
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `actions/es_errors.ts` | New `isUnavailableShardsException` checker |
| `actions/index.ts` | New `UnavailableShardsException` interface +
`ActionErrorTypeMap` entry |
| `actions/bulk_overwrite_transformed_documents.ts` | Detect unavailable
shards in bulk response, return dedicated left value |
| `model/model.ts` | Handle with `delayRetryState(...,
Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)` for infinite retries |
| `zdt/.../outdated_documents_search_bulk_index.ts` | Same handling for
ZDT (shared function) |
| 3 test files | Unit + recovery tests |

## Test plan

- [x] `isUnavailableShardsException` unit tests (true/false/undefined
cases)
- [x] `bulkOverwriteTransformedDocuments` unit tests (all unavailable
shards, mixed with version conflicts, mixed with non-retryable)
- [x] Model unit tests for retry behavior in both
`REINDEX_SOURCE_TO_TEMP_INDEX_BULK` and
`TRANSFORMED_DOCUMENTS_BULK_INDEX`
- [x] Multi-step recovery tests (retry on error -> succeed on next
attempt -> reset retry state)
- [x] Typecheck passes
- [x] Lint passes
- [x] All 169 model tests pass, all 8 bulk_overwrite tests pass, all 23
es_errors tests pass

<details>
<summary>PRD</summary>

# PRD: Handle unavailable_shards_exception as retryable in SO v2
migrations

## Introduction

Saved object v2 migrations (non-ZDT) fail with a fatal error when the
`bulkOverwriteTransformedDocuments` step encounters an
`unavailable_shards_exception` from Elasticsearch. This happens because
the bulk write uses `wait_for_active_shards: 'all'`, and when not all
shard copies are available, ES returns `unavailable_shards_exception`
errors in the bulk response items. These errors are not recognized as
retryable -- they fall through to a `throw new
Error(JSON.stringify(errors))` which terminates the migration fatally.

The fix is to recognize `unavailable_shards_exception` as a retryable
error in `bulkOverwriteTransformedDocuments` and handle it with infinite
retry attempts (matching the `wait_for_task_completion_timeout`
precedent), allowing the migration to retry with exponential backoff
indefinitely until shards become available.

## Goals

- Prevent fatal migration failures caused by temporarily unavailable
Elasticsearch shards
- Reuse the existing `delayRetryState` exponential backoff
infrastructure with infinite retries (like
`wait_for_task_completion_timeout`)
- Keep the fix scoped to `bulkOverwriteTransformedDocuments` only (not
ZDT migrations)

## User Stories

### US-001: Detect unavailable_shards_exception in bulk response errors
**Description:** As the migration framework, I need to identify
`unavailable_shards_exception` errors in bulk response items so that I
can treat them as retryable instead of fatal.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [x] Add an `isUnavailableShardsException` type checker in
`es_errors.ts`
- [x] The checker matches bulk response item errors where `type` is
`unavailable_shards_exception`
- [x] Typecheck passes

### US-002: Return unavailable_shards error from
bulkOverwriteTransformedDocuments
**Description:** As the migration framework, when
`bulkOverwriteTransformedDocuments` encounters
`unavailable_shards_exception` errors in the bulk response, I want to
return a dedicated left value so the state machine can retry with
infinite attempts.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [x] Check if all remaining errors are `unavailable_shards_exception`
before the throw fallthrough
- [x] Return `Either.left({ type: 'unavailable_shards_exception' as
const, message })` with descriptive message
- [x] Add `unavailable_shards_exception` to the return type union
- [x] Mixed error types still cause fatal failure
- [x] Typecheck and lint pass

### US-003: Handle unavailable_shards_exception in the migration model
with infinite retries
**Description:** As the migration framework, when the model receives an
`unavailable_shards_exception` response, I want to retry with
exponential backoff and infinite attempts.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [x] Handle in `REINDEX_SOURCE_TO_TEMP_INDEX_BULK` and
`TRANSFORMED_DOCUMENTS_BULK_INDEX` state handlers
- [x] Use `delayRetryState(state, message, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)` for
indefinite retries
- [x] Typecheck and lint pass

### US-004: Unit tests for unavailable_shards_exception handling
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [x] es_errors checker tests
- [x] bulkOverwriteTransformedDocuments tests (3 scenarios)
- [x] Model retry behavior tests for both states
- [x] All tests pass

### US-005: Integration-style recovery tests
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [x] Multi-step model tests simulating retry-then-succeed flow
- [x] Verifies migration does not enter FATAL state
- [x] Verifies migration recovers and progresses after retry
- [x] Tests pass

## Functional Requirements

- FR-1: `isUnavailableShardsException(error)` returns true when
`error.type === 'unavailable_shards_exception'`
- FR-2: `bulkOverwriteTransformedDocuments` returns `Either.left({ type:
'unavailable_shards_exception', message })` when all remaining bulk
errors are unavailable shards
- FR-3: Model handles with `delayRetryState(state, message,
Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)` for infinite retries with exponential backoff
(2s, 4s, 8s... up to 64s cap)
- FR-4: Logging happens automatically via existing retry logging
infrastructure

## Non-Goals

- No changes to the retry infrastructure itself
- No changes to `wait_for_active_shards: 'all'` setting
- No handling of `unavailable_shards_exception` in other actions

## Technical Considerations

- A dedicated `unavailable_shards_exception` error type (rather than
reusing `retryable_es_client_error`) is needed so the model can apply
infinite retries specifically for this case
- `bulkOverwriteTransformedDocuments` is shared between v2 and ZDT
migrations, so the ZDT model also needed updating
- ES client for migrations uses `maxRetries: 0` so the state machine
handles all retries

</details>

## Description

Adds tests verifying the rate limiting (cooldown) mechanisms in the Stellar-Save Soroban smart contract that prevent spam and abuse.

The rate limiting logic was already implemented in `create_group` and `join_group`. This PR adds the missing test coverage described in the PR description.

## Key Changes

### Constants (already in `lib.rs`)
- `GROUP_CREATION_COOLDOWN = 300` (5 minutes)
- `GROUP_JOIN_COOLDOWN = 120` (2 minutes)

### Storage Keys (already in `storage.rs`)
- `UserKey::LastGroupCreation(Address)`
- `UserKey::LastGroupJoin(Address)`

### Error (already in `error.rs`)
- `StellarSaveError::RateLimitExceeded = 9005`

### Tests Added
- `test_group_creation_rate_limit` — second create within 300s cooldown fails with error 9005
- `test_group_creation_rate_limit_after_cooldown` — create succeeds after cooldown expires
- `test_group_join_rate_limit` — second join within 120s cooldown fails with error 9005
- `test_group_join_rate_limit_after_cooldown` — join succeeds after cooldown expires
- `test_rate_limit_is_per_user` — cooldowns are independent per user address

## Verification
- Contract compiles successfully: `cargo build --lib`
- All rate limiting tests verify the functionality

## Related Issue
Fixes #270 - Add rate limiting to prevent spam

body:
…apping

The error correction was using interpolated fractional coordinates (planeLeft + (px+0.5)*scale) which differed by ~1px from what pierrec/msdf uses internally (floor(bounds.Min) + pixelIndex). This caused winding number checks to misclassify pixels, producing shadow/dithering artifacts.

Now uses the exact same floor-based mapping as pierrec/msdf's SDF loop, ensuring the winding number test agrees with the MSDF distance values.

author: octo-patch
body:
## Summary

Add [MiniMax](https://www.minimax.io/) as a first-class LLM provider in prompttools, enabling users to test and compare MiniMax models alongside existing providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Mistral.

### Changes

- **New `MiniMaxChatExperiment` class** (`prompttools/experiment/experiments/minimax_chat_experiment.py`): Extends the `Experiment` base class using MiniMax's OpenAI-compatible chat completions API via the `openai` library (already a dependency) with custom `base_url`
- **Supported models**: `MiniMax-M2.7`, `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, `MiniMax-M2.5`, `MiniMax-M2.5-highspeed`
- **Temperature clamping**: Automatically clamps temperature values to MiniMax's required (0.0, 1.0] range
- **DEBUG mode**: Mock function added for testing without API calls
- **Playground integration**: Registered as "MiniMax Chat" in the Streamlit playground UI
- **Comprehensive tests**: 33 unit tests + 3 integration tests covering initialization, parameter handling, mock responses, playground registration, and live API calls
- **README**: Updated supported integrations list

### Usage

```python
from prompttools.experiment import MiniMaxChatExperiment

messages = [
    [{"role": "user", "content": "Tell me a joke."}],
    [{"role": "user", "content": "Is 17077 a prime number?"}],
]

experiment = MiniMaxChatExperiment(
    model=["MiniMax-M2.7", "MiniMax-M2.5"],
    messages=messages,
    temperature=[0.5],
)
experiment.run()
experiment.visualize()
```

## Test Plan

- [x] All 33 unit tests passing (import, init, temperature clamping, mock, playground registration, cartesian product, DEBUG mode)
- [x] All 3 integration tests passing with live MiniMax API calls (single completion, model comparison, evaluate)
- [x] Follows existing provider patterns (Mistral, OpenAI)

## Summary
- **Bug:** In the "Add Custom Model" dialog, clicking any checkbox in "Supported Parameters" (Top P, Top K, Reasoning) or "Multimodal Support" (Files, Audio) only toggles the first item (Temperature / Images)
- **Root cause:** `HorizontalFormControl` uses Chakra v3's `Field.Root` + `Field.Label`, which assigns a single `id` to the first form control descendant. Multiple checkboxes inside one `Field.Root` all compete for that ID, so clicks always route to the first checkbox
- **Fix:** Replace `HorizontalFormControl` with plain `Box` layout (using `role="group"` + `aria-label` for accessibility) for the two checkbox group sections. Text input fields remain in `HorizontalFormControl` since they each have exactly one input

author: binhnt92
body:
## Summary

Prevents the OpenAI-compatible API server from leaking internal exception details to callers and hardens API key comparison against timing side-channel attacks.

## Problem

**Error leakage:** All 12 exception handlers in `api_server.py` return raw `str(e)` to API callers — either via `_openai_error(f"Internal server error: {e}")` (4 chat/responses endpoints) or `{"error": str(e)}` (8 cron endpoints). Python exception messages can contain internal file paths, database error details, library version info, and partial stack traces. Any OpenAI-compatible frontend (Open WebUI, LobeChat, etc.) receives these in the response body.

**Timing-unsafe auth:** API key comparison at line 347 uses `==` instead of `hmac.compare_digest()`, allowing timing side-channel brute-force.

## Fixes

**1. Error sanitization — 12 locations** (`gateway/platforms/api_server.py`)

- 4 chat/responses endpoints: stripped exception from `_openai_error()`, keeping generic message. `logger.error()` already exists above each handler for diagnostics.
- 8 cron endpoints: replaced `{"error": str(e)}` with generic message, added `logger.exception()` for server-side diagnostics.

**2. Timing-safe auth** (`gateway/platforms/api_server.py`)

Replaced `token == self._api_key` with `hmac.compare_digest(token, self._api_key)`.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `gateway/platforms/api_server.py` | Add `import hmac`, use `compare_digest` for auth, strip `str(e)` from all 12 error responses, add `logger.exception` to cron handlers |
| `tests/gateway/test_api_server_security.py` | 3 new tests: verify `compare_digest` in source, no exception interpolation in `_openai_error`, no `str(e)` in cron responses |

## Tests

```
3 passed
```

## Describe the changes in the pull request

This removes the `RsValueFFI` layer which is not needed anymore now that `RsValue` is switched over to Rust.

#### Mark if applicable

If a release note is required (bug fix / new feature / enhancement), describe the **user impact** of this PR in the title.

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches multiple Rust↔C FFI boundaries (rlookup/sorting vector/value comparisons) and changes C header signatures and pointer layouts; bugs could surface as refcount/ownership or ABI mismatches at runtime.
> 
> **Overview**
> Removes the `RSValueFFI` wrapper layer (and its `c_ffi_impl` feature) and updates Rust code to use `RsValue` plus `SharedRsValue` for refcounted shared ownership across `rlookup`, `sorting_vector`, and related tests.
> 
> Updates the C FFI surface and generated headers to pass raw `RSValue*`/`const RSValue*` (including sorting-vector slice representation), adds `query_error` plumbing where needed, and routes comparisons through new helpers (`compare_with_query_error_to_int`, `compare_on_equality_only`) while dropping the exported `RSValueSize` macro/constant and related bindgen header inclusion.

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure the console reflects actual routing state instead of optimistic logging for F2F handoffs.
- Detect and react when `panda_f2f_bridge.hard_route_branch` fails or errors instead of assuming success.
- Provide a deterministic fallback via `xr_meet.override_dialog` and a clear "no route" log when no routing can be applied.

### Description
- Wrap the call to `panda_f2f_bridge.hard_route_branch` in `pcall` and capture the returned `route_applied` result to determine real success.
- Only log bridge routing success when the call both executes and returns a truthy value, and log an explicit failure otherwise including `npc_id`, `conv_id`, and `turn`.
- Attempt `xr_meet.override_dialog(c.npc_id, "panda_f2f_hub_dialog")` as a fallback when bridge routing fails and `xr_meet` is available, with an accompanying fallback log.
- Add an explicit `no route available` log when neither bridge routing nor `xr_meet` fallback can be applied.

### Testing

author: scylladbbot
body:
ERMs created in `calculate_vnode_effective_replication_map` have RF computed based
on the old token metadata during a topology change. The reading replicas, however,
are computed based on the new token metadata (`target_token_metadata`) when
`read_new` is true. That can create a mismatch for EverywhereStrategy during some
topology changes - RF can be equal to the number of reading replicas +-1. During
bootstrap, this can cause the
`everywhere_replication_strategy::sanity_check_read_replicas` check to fail in
debug mode.

We fix the check in this commit by allowing one more reading replica when
`read_new` is true.

Fixes https://scylladb.atlassian.net/browse/SCYLLADB-1147

Backport to all supported branches, as tests can fail there due to the issue being
fixed.

- (cherry picked from commit 503a6e2d7efa39a63e9bfc154c0780ff9a2fda9c)

author: tstirrat
body:
## Thinking Path

- Paperclip orchestrates AI agents for zero-human companies
- Every agent that has the Paperclip skill gets `SKILL.md` injected into their context on **every heartbeat run**
- The skill was 365 lines / 23KB — this bloats context windows across every agent, every run, at significant token cost
- Most of the content in the skill is only needed in specific, infrequent situations (project setup, OpenClaw invites, import/export, etc.)
- So we can apply **progressive disclosure**: keep only the heartbeat procedure and critical rules inline, and move situational content to reference files that agents read on demand
- But we need to be careful not to regress agent reliability — some content was previously hardened into the body after field failures
- This PR reduces the main skill body by 60% while preserving all critical inline content and routing agents to `references/` files via conditional "When X, read Y" pointers

## What Changed

**`skills/paperclip/SKILL.md`** — reduced from 365 lines (23KB) to 145 lines (11KB):

- **Kept verbatim:** frontmatter, heartbeat concept, authentication, Steps 1–9, Critical Rules
- **Compressed inline:** Comment Style (retained ticket-link rule, company-prefix rule, and full URL pattern list — these were hardened across multiple commits due to field reliability issues, so kept close)
- **Compressed inline:** Planning (retained key rules; moved API flow details to reference)
- **Removed from body:** Key Endpoints table (fully covered by `api-reference.md`), Project Setup, OpenClaw Invite, Company Skills inline section, Instructions Path, Import/Export, Searching Issues, Self-Test Playbook
- **Added:** References table — `| When... | Read |` — conditional pointers so agents load detail only when the situation applies

**`skills/paperclip/references/workflows.md`** (new file, 198 lines):

- Receives all moved content with H2 anchors for deep-linking
- Sections: Comment Style Details, Planning, Project Setup, OpenClaw Invite, Instructions Path, Import/Export, Searching Issues, Self Test

## Why This Matters

Every agent with the Paperclip skill pays the full 23KB context cost on every heartbeat, even for simple runs (pick up task → do work → comment → exit). The majority of that content is never needed in a typical run. This change reduces the per-heartbeat context overhead significantly, which compounds across all agents and all runs.

A secondary benefit: a smaller skill means **shorter, less cluttered agent comments on issues**. When the skill is large, agents tend to over-explain and reference content they've just been primed with. A leaner skill produces more focused, actionable comments — which improves the signal-to-noise ratio in issue threads that humans and other agents read.

## How It Was Made

The optimization was done using the [`skill-creator`](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/tree/master/skills/skill-creator) skill, which is designed for exactly this kind of structured skill reduction — analysing what belongs inline vs. behind progressive disclosure, preserving reliability-critical content, and wiring up conditional reference pointers.

## Git History Check

Before compressing, checked `git log --follow -p skills/paperclip/SKILL.md` to identify content deliberately hardened into the body:

- **Comment Style** was strengthened across 3 separate commits after agents posted malformed links in production — kept the full URL pattern list inline rather than behind a reference pointer
- **Critical Rules** and **Steps 1–9** were left entirely untouched
- Content with no history of reliability issues (Project Setup, OpenClaw, etc.) was moved to references

## Verification — Local Dev Testing

Tested against a local Paperclip instance (COR company, CEO agent, claude-sonnet-4-6).

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| Comment style: ticket links + prefixed URLs | ✅ Agent posted `[COR-1](/COR/issues/COR-1)` — correct markdown link, correct prefix |
| Checkout before working | ✅ `POST /api/issues/{id}/checkout` with `X-Paperclip-Run-Id` confirmed in run log |
| Blocked status reporting | ✅ Status set to `blocked`, clear comment explaining blocker and who needs to act |
| Blocked-task dedup | ✅ Second heartbeat correctly skipped — own prior comment, no new context |
| Clean exit when no work | ✅ Exited cleanly with no API mutations |

All tests behaviorally neutral — no regressions observed.

## Risks

- Agents that encounter a situation requiring a reference file (e.g. project setup) must follow the pointer and read `workflows.md` — if they skip the pointer, they will have less guidance. This is mitigated by the "When X, read Y" framing being explicit and conditional.
- The Comment Style rules were the highest-risk area given their history; they were retained inline to avoid any regression there.

author: gitricko
body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/gitricko/openclaw-webtop/security/code-scanning/1](https://github.com/gitricko/openclaw-webtop/security/code-scanning/1)

In general, the problem is fixed by explicitly specifying `permissions` for the `GITHUB_TOKEN` either at the workflow root (applies to all jobs without their own `permissions`) or per job. Here, `push-to-ghcr` already declares `permissions`, but `build-test` (and the workflow root) do not. To avoid changing existing behavior while enforcing least privilege, we should add a root-level `permissions` block with `contents: read`, which is sufficient for `actions/checkout` and does not interfere with `push-to-ghcr` (its own `permissions` block will override the root).

Concretely:
- Edit `.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml`.
- After the `name:` line and before `on:`, add:
  ```yaml
  permissions:
    contents: read
  ```
- Leave the existing `permissions` block in `push-to-ghcr` unchanged.

No other methods, imports, or definitions are needed; this is a pure YAML configuration change.

| Two identical Lenovo E24-28 (HDMI-A-1, DP-3) | Both: `Lenovo Group Limited:E24-28:16843009` | `...16843009/HDMI-A-1` and `...16843009/DP-3` |

| Tiling/snapping | Only works on primary | Works on both monitors |

## Fallback scenarios (backward compat)
- **Monitor moved to different port**: Connector suffix won't match, falls back to EDID base match
- **Old config without suffix + now-duplicate monitors**: Reverse fallback matches base ID (returns first match)
- **Suffixed config + only one monitor now**: Base ID match succeeds (no suffix needed when unique)

## Summary

- Merge the `gh-webhook` functionality into the `watch` command as optional `--webhook-port` / `--webhook-secret` flags
- The watch command now runs an async `tokio::select!` event loop that multiplexes a timer and an optional webhook channel
- Both timer-triggered and webhook-triggered cycles reset the timer, preventing redundant runs
- Webhook-triggered cycles skip `git ls-remote` polling and run all hosts directly
- Concurrent webhook events during an active cycle are dropped (channel capacity 1)
- The `gh-webhook` subcommand and `--script` mode are removed entirely
- Adds 11 new tests (5 webhook handler, 6 CLI validation) — 44 total, all passing, zero clippy warnings

body:
### Motivation
- Evitar que la tabla quede filtrada por el último código luego de crear una prenda y mantener la lista completa por defecto. 
- Hacer que las acciones sensibles (`eliminar`, `archivar`, `restaurar`, importaciones) usen endpoints protegidos por sesión admin. 
- Corregir el formato de payload esperado por el backend para que `delete/archive/restore` realmente ejecuten las operaciones en Sheets.

### Description
- Se creó `api/admin.js` que reusa la lógica de `lib/api/core.js` y expone las acciones admin protegidas por `requireAdminSession` (`prendas-delete`, `prendas-archive`, `prendas-restore`, `prendas-archived-list`, `prendas-import-corrections`, `prendas-admin`).
- Se ajustó `api/core.js` para exportar `sendOk`, `sendErr`, `requireAdminSession` y `ADMIN_SESSION_REQUIRED_MESSAGE`, y se removió el enrutamiento de las acciones admin de prendas dejando `prendas-create` pública (`/api/core?action=prendas-create`).
- Frontend: en `public/index.html` se añadió `callPrendasAdminApi` y se reenrutan las llamadas sensibles a `/api/admin`; además se cambió el payload de `deletePrendaInSheets`, `archivePrendaInSheets` y `restorePrendaInSheets` para enviar `{ codigo }` como objeto.
- UX post-guardado: en el flujo de guardado (tras `await createPrendaInSheets(payload)`) se limpian `prendasSearchInput` y `prendasSearch`, se resetea `prendasState.queryKey = ""`, se mantiene la recarga con `await loadPrendasPage({ reset: true, reason: "save-garment" })` y se preserva la vista del bloque "Código generado" sin tocar la generación ni el guardado en Sheets.
- Se actualizó `public/shared/corrections-adapter.js` para apuntar `prendas-import-corrections` a `/api/admin`.

### Testing
- Se ejecutó `node --check api/core.js` y la comprobación de sintaxis pasó correctamente. 
- Se ejecutó `node --check api/admin.js` y la comprobación de sintaxis pasó correctamente. 
- Se verificaron referencias y rutas con `rg` (`prendas-delete`, `prendas-archive`, `prendas-restore`, `prendas-archived-list`, `prendas-import-corrections`) y confirmaron que las llamadas sensibles ahora usan `/api/admin` y que `prendas-create` sigue en `/api/core`.
- Se validó en el código cliente que las llamadas a `delete/archive/restore` envían el objeto `{ codigo }` y que después de guardar se limpia la búsqueda y se recarga la lista completa; estas comprobaciones son estáticas (sin navegador) y pasaron en los chequeos realizados.

author: yeraze
body:
## Summary
- Pins ARMv7 Dockerfile base image to `node:22.22.1-bookworm-slim`
- Fixes the same 4 Snyk vulnerabilities from PR #2445 (critical zlib overflow, medium systemd, low gnutls)

## Why not trixie-slim?
Snyk's PR #2445 proposed `node:22.22.1-trixie-slim`, but that image **does not publish an `arm/v7` manifest** — it only has amd64, arm64, ppc64le, and s390x. This would break ARMv7 builds for Raspberry Pi 2/3.

`node:22.22.1-bookworm-slim` has full `arm/v7` support and is based on the same Debian release we were already using (bookworm), just with a pinned Node.js version for security fixes.

author: huyhoang171106
body:
## Summary

`addr_to_int()` converts dot-separated parts with `int()` but never validates octet count/range. Inputs like `999.1.1.1` are accepted, and later conversions (e.g., via `int_to_addr`) can wrap values with `& 0xff`, producing a different IP than the original. This is silent data corruption in address handling and can lead to wrong trail matching/blocking behavior.

## Files changed

- `core/addr.py` (modified)

- Not run in this environment.


Closes #19536

## What
Fix EsSitemapReader to use AOT-safe JSON construction instead of anonymous types that fail under PublishAot/PublishTrimmed.

## Why
The assembler sitemap command fails with a 400 from ES in CI. In AOT mode, System.Text.Json cannot serialize anonymous types via reflection — the serialized body is malformed (empty objects). Locally it works because `dotnet run` uses the full runtime with reflection-based serialization.

## How
- Replace anonymous types in `BuildSearchBody` with `JsonObject`/`JsonArray` from `System.Text.Json.Nodes` (AOT-safe)
- Replace anonymous type in `ClosePitAsync` with `Dictionary<string, string>`
- Use `PostData.String()` instead of `PostData.Serializable()` since JSON is now pre-built

author: d-stacks
body:
# Fast Trusted Relay (FTR) Implementation

## Summary

**Note: This is a WIP draft PR, published for testing and discussion visibility, and not considered stable!**

Introduces a **Fast Trusted Relay** (FTR) network protocol for Kaspa, enabling low-latency block propagation via a custom push based UDP transport protocol with Reed-Solomon Forward Error Correction (FEC). Designed for trusted operators (mining pools, infrastructure providers, or even just altruistic actors) to achieve minimal block transfer latency across geographically distributed nodes. Although this directly profits those that require low-latency block propagation, any fast relay overlay, also indirectly helps the global kaspa network reduce propagation. Further use-cases may include satellite communications, where RTTs can inherently become a limiting factor, or faster communication between nodes situated within one data-center. The application of the customizable FEC also facilitates adopting this protocol in potentially lossy network conditions.

Furthermore, Fast Relay networks are oftentimes exclusive services offered by enterprise for enterprise, which can easily compound, for example, pool advantages over individual solo miners, by offering an open source easily accessible Fast Relay option on the node, free for anyone to use, we limit such centralized advantages and also help facilitate more such overlays to establish themselves on the kaspa network.

The main observable changes are that logs will display the number of blocks propagated via the fast relay network, alongside the normal blocks added logs, as such:

```
2026-03-26 14:14:40.849+01:00 [INFO ] Accepted 9 blocks ...2ab529f31b82379f60d1799b3d72d06eac3ca77b29b1f8dfb8dde3ec7737a4ac via relay
2026-03-26 14:14:40.849+01:00 [INFO ] Accepted 5 blocks ...2afc49022f1c41890b182252b80844992afcac58deb1f2b6661e5d1049e17d4b via trusted relay
```

One key limitation of this protocol is that due to its push-based nature it cannot function in isolation, and should / must be used together with standard relay. This is quintessential for resolving protocol aspects such as orphan resolution, etc... Currently, adding a peer to the FTR network will automatically add the peer to the standard relay as well, in order to facilitate such operations.

Although this PR is a far-shot away from replacing our standard tcp relay, adopting and adapting such a custom udp protocol could potentially be an entry point for gathering data and experience for such a maneuver, many projects, such as solana's Turbine block propagation, already use highly customized and optimized udp transport layers, in order to reduce latency.

## Motivation

Standard P2P block relay (TCP-based with request-response semantics) introduces latency that compounds across multiple hops and during network congestion. For operations where latency directly impacts orphan rates and revenue, a dedicated push-based relay with erasure coding provides significant advantages:

- **Push-based propagation**: No round-trip handshakes per block
- **Loss tolerance**: FEC allows recovery even when packets are lost in lossy network conditions
- **UDP based**: fire and forget on a per packet basis, with 0 rtts in the protocol. 
- **Parallel processing**: UDP Pipeline is fully configurable to be multi-threaded. 

One trade-off is that the FTR bypasses block signaling and propagates whole blocks. Furthermore, FEC increases the bandwidth usage, which quickly compounds with the number of peers in the network. As such, a large network bandwidth should be a prerequisite to run such a FTR network. That being said, facilitating 10-20 peers (which should easily be enough for a good globally dispersed network) on a 1Gbit or 10Gbit connection should easily be sustainable, As should a small handful of peers on even more limited bandwidth.

## Example Usage:

`./kaspad --trusted-relay-secret=[your secret] --trusted-relay-incoming=[list of peer ips we expect to get packets from] --trusted-relay-outgoing=[list of peer ips we wish to push packets to] --externalip=[your ip]`

Establishing a connection might take a while and connection re-attempts happen every 30 secs. 

Note: 
1) Akin to public nodes, using the FTR requires port forwarding, to receive packets (not to send). 
2) The default OS max send & receive port buffer sizes may not suffice to properly run the FTR. As such, this value needs to be increased with admin privileges. Currently I am running with 32 MB without issues (although sizes can depend on the number of inbound / outbound FTR peers and other config settings).

To increase these limits on Linux (in this example to 32 MB) the following can be run:

receive buffer:
`sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=33554432`
send buffer:
`sudo sysctl -w net.core.wmem_max=33554432`
  
## Architecture

### Two-Plane Design

| Plane | Transport | Purpose |
|-------|-----------|---------|
| **Control** | TCP (port 16113) | Handshake, peer management, ready-state signaling |
| **Data** | UDP (port 16114) | Transport Encoding and Decoding of Individual UDP Packets / Block fragments |

### Data Plane Pipeline

```
UDP Socket
    ↓
Collector (packet ingestion)
    ↓ [route by fragment_index % verifiers]
Verifier (HMAC validation, deduplication)
    ├→ Reassembler (fragment pooling, FEC trigger)
    │       ↓
    │   Decoder (Reed-Solomon recovery, pool -> block)
    │       ↓
    │   recv_block() → exit to external code. 
    │
    └→ Relay Worker (forward packet to other outbound peers)

Standard p2p flow
    ↓
Broadcaster (encode and fragment block, forward packets to outbound peers)
```

Note: The stack is designed upon crossbeam worker threads, and can easily be multithreaded in high load environments.

## Key Features

### Reed-Solomon FEC Encoding

- Default: k=16 data fragments, m=4 parity fragments per generation.
- Receiver needs only k of (k+m) fragments to recover data
- Tolerates ~20% packet loss by default configuration, but can be adapted.
- SIMD-accelerated via `reed-solomon-simd` crate (although actual benefits compared to other crates have not been benchmarked)

### HMAC-SHA256 Authentication

- Offers basic DDoS protection.
- Per-fragment MAC: `hmac(secret, header ‖ payload)`
- TCP handshake: `hmac(secret, nonce ‖ direction ‖ udp_port)`
- Shared secret across trusted peer group

### IBD-Aware Control

- UDP transport is designed to be toggleable
- Auto-disabled during Initial Block Download (IBD)
- Re-enabled when node considers itself synced
- Prevents relaying blocks node cannot validate

## New Crate: `kaspa-trusted-relay`

### Module Structure

```
protocol/trusted_relay/src/
├── fast_trusted_relay.rs    # Core forward facing FastTrustedRelay struct
├── params.rs                # TransportParams, FragmentationConfig
├── error.rs                 # RelayErrors (Not fully implemented, currently errors are only logged)
├── model/
│   ├── ftr_block.rs         # FtrBlock wire format
│   └── fragments.rs         # FragmentHeader (36 bytes)
├── codec/
│   ├── encoder.rs           # FragmentGenerator (with FEC encoding)
│   ├── decoder.rs           # Reed-Solomon decoding
│   └── buffers.rs           # (specialized buffers for reassembly pooling)
└── servers/
    ├── auth.rs              # TokenAuthenticator
    ├── peer_directory.rs    # PeerInfo, PeerDirectory (shared between UDP transport and TCP control)
    ├── tcp_control/
    │   ├── tcp.rs           # TCP listener, handshake
    │   ├── hub.rs           # Peer registry, tcp event routing
    │   └── peer.rs          # Per-peer control loop
    └── udp_transport/
        ├── runtime.rs       # UDP TransportRuntime lifecycle
        └── pipeline/        # Worker threads for the udp packets
            ├── collector.rs    # UDP recv threads (collects the packets)
            ├── verification.rs # Data integrity checks + HM

PRs without prior testing will be closed. -->

## ✍️ Description
Container creation fails when Debian/Ubuntu/Alpine CDN mirrors are unreachable, serve corrupted data (hash mismatch), or lack valid SSL certificates — especially in Asia/India.

**Solution**
Three-phase mirror fallback: Global → Primary → Regional → Manual prompt. Scans TCP reachability first, picks 3 random working mirrors per phase. Detects Debian vs Ubuntu automatically and uses the correct mirror pool. Alpine gets its own 8-mirror fallback.

_Key decisions:_
- HTTP instead of HTTPS (most country mirrors lack valid SSL certs)
- Global-first order (regional CDN is usually the broken one)


## Example:
```bash
💡  apt-get update failed (deb.debian.org), trying alternate mirrors...
💡  Attempting mirror: ftp.jp.debian.org
⚠️  Mirror ftp.jp.debian.org failed (SSL/certificate error)
💡  Attempting mirror: ftp.it.debian.org
✔️  CDN set to ftp.it.debian.org: tests passed
✔️  Customized LXC Container
```

body:
✅ Phase 2 — Revisions, Acts & Timeline Support
This PR completes Phase 2 of the Flux‑First architecture.
It introduces Revisions, Acts, Commit/Draft semantics, and a Timeline viewer, all implemented in pure C# / no‑XAML and fully integrated with the existing AppBar + Widget framework from Phase 1.
This lays the foundation for trustworthy historical tracking and prepares the system for Phase 3 (Search + Auto‑Weaving).

🚀 Highlights
✅ 1. Revision Tracking (Append‑Only)
Adds full append‑only revision history to each Resource:

Revision(Edit) created on Save Draft
Revision(Promote) created on Commit
Automatic update of the Artifact snapshot to match the latest revision
Revision IDs increment atomically per resource
Revisions stored inside resource.Revisions[] (Mongo-native)

This enables transparent, chronological evolution of each Saying.

✅ 2. Acts (Commit / Draft / Supersede)
Adds an intent layer via Acts:

Act(Tentative) recorded when saving a draft
Act(Commit) recorded on commit
Act(Supersede) automatically applied to the previous commit when a new commit is made

This creates a clear, explicit semantic boundary between editing and deciding, and provides parent‑child relationships between interpretation states.

✅ 3. SayingService (Draft + Commit workflow)
Adds a dedicated service for all Saying‑related state changes:

SaveDraftAsync(resourceId, body)

Appends Revision(Edit)
Adds Act(Tentative)
Updates Artifact snapshot


CommitAsync(resourceId, body)

Appends Revision(Promote)
Adds Act(Commit)
Supersedes previous commit
Updates Artifact snapshot



This isolates all domain rules into one clean location.

✅ 4. Timeline Service
Adds a TimelineService that returns:

Full list of revisions, newest first
Full list of acts, grouped by revision

This powers the new Timeline window.

✅ 5. ResourceEditorWindow (Draft/Commit/Timeline Controls)
Adds a no‑XAML editor window for interactive Saying editing:

Multi-line Markdown editor
Save Draft
Commit
Timeline button inside the editor, not the AppBar
Optional keyboard shortcuts:

Ctrl+S — Save Draft
Ctrl+Enter — Commit
Ctrl+T — Timeline



The editor now behaves as the central workspace for reasoning over a resource.

✅ 6. Timeline Window
Adds a new TimelineWindow (pure C#) that displays:

Each revision (ID, kind, timestamp)
Associated Acts for each revision
Entries sorted newest-first

This gives visibility into how a resource has evolved over time and what decisions were made along the way.

✅ 7. Controller Integration
AppController now exposes:

CreateDraftNoteAsync() (fixed to insert a new Resource)
SaveDraftAsync(resourceId, body)
CommitAsync(resourceId, body)
LoadTimelineAsync(resourceId)

The AppBar now launches the ResourceEditor, which in turn launches Timeline windows with the correct ResourceId (no user prompts).

✅ 8. Mongo Integration Verified

Writes now persist correctly:

New resources
Revisions
Acts


MongoStatusWidget confirms:

✅ Connection
✅ Authentication
✅ Write access


The earlier issue (resources not being inserted) was fixed by updating CreateDraftNoteAsync() to properly insert the Resource.


📁 Files Added / Updated
(High-level overview; no excess noise)

Domain Models: Revision, Act, Resource updated
Stores: Updated ResourceStore for append-only revision & act writes
SayingService: Draft + Commit workflow
TimelineService: Revision/Act retrieval
Windows: ResourceEditorWindow, TimelineWindow (pure C#)
Controller: Revisions/Acts APIs
AppBarWindow: launches editors; Timeline moved into editor
Mongo Status Widget (debug aid)


✅ Phase 2 Complete
All Phase 2 goals are now met:

Revision history ✅
Acts layer (Commit/Draft/Supersede) ✅
Timeline viewer ✅
Editor integration ✅
Controller + Mongo integration ✅
No‑XAML UI ✅

System is now ready for Phase 3: Search + Auto-Weaving.

body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a new `getEffectivePlan()` function to handle race conditions during the Stripe subscription checkout flow, where the subscription row exists with a `stripePriceId` before the webhook updates the user's plan in the database.

## Key Changes
- **New function `getEffectivePlan()`**: Extracts the subscription-aware plan resolution logic from `getProfilePlan()` into a reusable function that:
  - Returns the database plan if it's not "trial"
  - Falls back to deriving the plan from `stripePriceId` if the plan is "trial" but a subscription row exists
  - Returns "trial" if the price ID is unrecognized
  
- **Updated `api-key-actions.ts`**: Replaced `getPlan()` calls with `getEffectivePlan()` in both `listApiKeys()` and `createApiKey()` to ensure API key access checks use the effective plan during the subscription race condition window

- **Simplified `getProfilePlan()`**: Removed the inline subscription-aware logic (now delegated to `getEffectivePlan()`) while maintaining the same display behavior

- **Comprehensive test coverage**: Added 4 test cases for `getEffectivePlan()` covering:
  - Non-trial plans (no subscription lookup needed)
  - Trial plans without subscription rows
  - Trial plans with subscription rows (race condition handling)
  - Unrecognized price IDs (fallback to trial)
  
  Also added a test case in `api-key-actions.test.ts` to verify the race condition is handled correctly

## Implementation Details
- The function queries the `subscriptions` table to check for an existing subscription row with `stripePriceId`
- Uses `planFromPriceId()` to derive the plan from the Stripe price ID
- Maintains backward compatibility: feature gates continue to read from the database plan, while UI and access checks use the effective plan
- All mocks properly configured to support the new dependency chain

body:
## Summary

Complete implementation of distributed stratum evaluation for wirelog columnar backend, enabling multi-worker parallel evaluation of datalog programs with coordinator-driven frontier-based skip optimization.

**Issue References**: #318, #313

## Key Features

- **Multi-worker Parallelism**: Partition-based evaluation across W workers with per-worker session isolation
- **Coordinator-Driven Architecture**: Central coordinator manages iteration loop, barrier synchronization, and convergence detection
- **Hash-Partitioned Exchange**: EXCHANGE operator support with broadcast fallback for non-partitioned rules (e.g., transitive closure)
- **Frontier Skip Optimization**: Reuse convergence information across session snapshots to reduce redundant iterations
- **Zero Overhead for W=1**: Direct delegation to col_eval_stratum avoids TDD overhead for single-worker case

## Implementation Summary

### Phase Breakdown (9 atomic commits)

1. **Phase 0**: Scaffold col_eval_stratum_tdd with W=1 fast path
2. **Phase 1**: Core data structures (tdd_init_workers, dispatch, merge)  
3. **Phase 2**: Barrier synchronization and worker sub-pass evaluation
4. **Phase 3**: Hash-partitioned exchange operator integration
5. **Phase 4-4b**: Convergence detection, frontier persistence, and helper functions

### Test Coverage

- **16 new tests** in test_tdd_*.c files
- **W=1/2/4 correctness validation**: Distributed results match single-worker baseline
- **Coverage**: Non-recursive paths, recursive convergence, cyclic graphs, deep chains, exchange scatter/gather

## Verification

- ✅ All 104 tests pass (1 expected fail, 0 failures)
- ✅ Compilation: Clean (uncrustify formatted)
- ✅ TDD approach: Each phase has accompanying test commits
- ✅ Atomic commits: Each phase is logically independent and compilable
- ✅ No regressions: All existing tests continue to pass

## Files Modified

- wirelog/columnar/eval.c: ~1200 LOC added (8 functions + documentation)
- wirelog/columnar/ops.c: 2 bug fixes (delta heuristic, consolidation guard)
- wirelog/columnar/internal.h: 4 fields added to col_session_t
- tests/test_tdd_*.c: 16 new unit tests (3 files)

## Design Decisions

1. **Coordinator-driven outer loop** simplifies convergence detection
2. **Per-worker delta relations** with shared frontier tracking
3. **Hash-partitioned exchange with broadcast fallback** for semantic correctness
4. **Helper functions** for code clarity and maintainability

author: lmenezes
body:
## Problem

Pipeline redirect results (overflow, async merge) use raw topic strings, bypassing the outputs abstraction that already handles events, heatmaps, and ingestion warnings. This prevents redirects from leveraging the flexible broker and topic configuration that outputs provide — particularly important for multi-broker deployments where overflow traffic needs to route to a different Kafka cluster.

## Changes

- Replace `redirect('reason', topicString)` with `redirect('reason', OVERFLOW_OUTPUT)` — redirects now target named outputs instead of raw Kafka topics
- Thread redirect type `R` through the entire pipeline infrastructure (`PipelineResult<T, R>`, `Pipeline`, `BatchPipeline`, all builders) with compile-time safety and no type casts
- `feed()` now only accepts `OkResultWithContext` — enforces that pipeline input is always fresh OK results, not recycled non-OK results
- `BranchingPipelineBuilder` widens `R` per branch call, accumulating redirect types from all branches
- Add `OVERFLOW_OUTPUT` and `ASYNC_OUTPUT` to output definitions with configurable topics via env vars
- Remove dead `overflowTopic` from subpipeline configs, `PERSON_MERGE_ASYNC_TOPIC` from pipeline options, and `dlqTopic` from `IngestionConsumer`
- Add `createMockPipeline` and `createOkContext` test helpers
- Update living docs (chapters 1 and 7) to reflect named redirect outputs

### Deployment

Before merging, set these env vars in all environments to match the existing topic overrides:

- `INGESTION_OUTPUT_OVERFLOW_TOPIC` — same value as `INGESTION_CONSUMER_OVERFLOW_TOPIC`
- `INGESTION_OUTPUT_ASYNC_TOPIC` — same value as `PERSON_MERGE_ASYNC_TOPIC`
- `INGESTION_OUTPUT_DLQ_TOPIC` — same value as `INGESTION_CONSUMER_DLQ_TOPIC`

## How did you test this code?

- All 310 pipeline tests pass
- Zero TypeScript errors, zero type casts in production pipeline code
- All redirect output names use typed constants, no string literals

## Publish to changelog?

No

## Docs update

No external docs needed — living test docs updated in-repo.

body:
Builds a full NY Yankees schedule viewer from scratch on an empty repo — upcoming games with infinite scroll, completed games with scores, and live broadcast info pulled from the MLB Stats API.

## Stack
- **Next.js 16** (App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4)
- **MLB Stats API** (`statsapi.mlb.com`, team ID 147) — gracefully falls back to mock schedule data when API is unreachable
- Custom CSS with Yankees navy (`#0C2340`) / white / gold (`#C4A862`) palette; responsive at 600px

## Pages

### `/` — Upcoming Games
- First load: today's next game pinned at top with "⚾ Next Game" label in a dark featured card, plus 5 more below
- Infinite scroll loads 5 additional games per trigger (IntersectionObserver sentinel)

### `/completed` — Completed Games
- Most-recent-first, scores visible, green **W** / red **L** badges per game
- Same infinite scroll pattern (20/page)

## Game Card Fields
Opponent · Date/time · **HOME** / **AWAY** · Venue · Broadcast networks (YES Network, ESPN, Apple TV+, etc.)

## Key Implementation Notes
- Active nav link highlighted in gold via `usePathname()` in a dedicated `NavLinks` client component — avoids making the entire layout a client component
- `hasMore` computed inside `setGames` updater callback to avoid stale closure on `games.length`
- API routes (`/api/games/upcoming`, `/api/games/completed`) proxy MLB API server-side; mock fallback is transparent to the UI via a `usingMockData` flag in the response

author: justsmth
body:
### Desccription of Changes:
`OCSPIntegrationTest` connects to live Amazon Trust Services OCSP responder endpoints, which are occasionally unavailable and cause spurious CI failures. This PR removes the `integration_test` binary from all normal CI test paths and moves it to a dedicated workflow that runs on every PR, on a daily schedule, and via manual dispatch. As a separate workflow, failures due to external endpoint issues will not block other CI checks.

### Call-outs:
There were four independent places where `integration_test` was invoked, all of which are removed:
- `util/all_tests.json` — consumed by the `run_tests` CMake target (the primary test path)
- `tests/ci/run_bsd_tests.sh` — direct invocation for BSD CI (this also had a NetBSD-specific `GTEST_FILTER` workaround for the same problem, which is now removed)
- `tests/ci/run_cross_tests.sh` — direct invocation for QEMU cross-compilation CI
- `tests/ci/run_cross_mingw_tests.sh` — direct invocation for MinGW cross-compilation CI

The `integration_test` binary also contains `OCSPRoundTripTest`, which uses a local mock and doesn't depend on external endpoints. It will now only run in the dedicated workflow as well.

### Testing:
The new workflow (`.github/workflows/ocsp-external-tests.yml`) can be verified via `workflow_dispatch`.
