author: fuddlesworth
body:
## Summary

This PR adds three major features to PlasmaZones autotiling:

### 1. Scripted Tiling Algorithms (Bring Your Own Layout)
- Users write custom tiling algorithms as JavaScript files
- Drop a `.js` in `~/.local/share/plasmazones/algorithms/` — it appears in the KCM immediately
- Hot-reload via QFileSystemWatcher (save file → layout updates live)
- System-installed scripts ship alongside built-in algorithms
- Ships 9 example algorithms: **Deck**, **Horizontal Deck**, **Tatami**, **Paper**, **Floating Center**, **Focus + Sidebar**, **Zen**, **Corner Master**, **Quadrant Priority**
- Persistent watchdog thread with 100ms timeout prevents runaway scripts
- Full `TilingAlgorithm` interface mapped to JS (metadata comments + optional function overrides)
- JS sandbox hardened: `eval`, `Function`, and `Function.prototype.constructor` frozen

### 2. Dwindle (Memory) Algorithm
- New `DwindleMemoryAlgorithm` with persistent BSP tree (`SplitTree`)
- Per-split ratios preserved across retiles — resize one split without affecting others
- Closing a window collapses its node; sibling ratios survive
- Opening a window splits the focused node (dwindle-style alternation)
- Float/unfloat correctly removes/reinserts tree leaves
- Lazy tree creation from current window order on first use
- Falls back to stateless dwindle when tree is unavailable
- Tree serialized in `TilingState::toJson()` for session persistence

### 3. Split Tree Exposed to JS Scripts
- Scripted algorithms can access the persistent split tree via `params.tree`
- Built-in `applyTreeGeometry(node, rect, gap)` helper injected into every JS engine
- One-line memory support: `if (params.tree) return applyTreeGeometry(params.tree, params.area, params.innerGap);`
- Read-only deep copy — scripts cannot corrupt the C++ tree
- Zero overhead for scripts that don't use `params.tree`

### 4. Generic Section Grouping in LayoutsPage
- Refactored from hardcoded aspect-ratio grouping to data-driven `sectionKey`/`sectionLabel`/`sectionOrder`
- Snapping layouts group by aspect ratio (as before)
- Autotile algorithms group by "Built-in" / "Custom"
- Shared `AlgorithmRegistry::sectionForAlgorithm()` helper (DRY)

### 5. Per-Algorithm Settings & Data-Driven UI
- Split ratio and master count stored per-algorithm (not global)
- Backwards-compatible migration from old centered-master fields
- Algorithm config controls driven by capability flags (`supportsSplitRatio`, `supportsMasterCount`, `centerLayout`, `zoneNumberDisplay`)
- Algorithm preview tracks combo selection immediately
- LayoutComboBox replaces text-only dropdown with visual previews

### Script Format
```js
// @name My Algorithm
// @description What it does
// @supportsMasterCount true
// @defaultMaxWindows 6

function calculateZones(params) {
    // params.windowCount, params.area, params.innerGap,
    // params.masterCount, params.splitRatio, params.minSizes
    // params.tree (optional — persistent split tree)
    return [{ x, y, width, height }, ...]
}
```

### Build
- Explicit `Qt6::Qml` dependency added for QJSEngine
- `data/algorithms/*.js` installed to `${KDE_INSTALL_DATADIR}/plasmazones/algorithms/`
- All packaging (RPM, Debian, Arch, Nix) verified — no packaging changes needed

### Code Quality (Post-Review)
- Persistent watchdog thread replaces detached thread-per-call (no thread accumulation under rapid resize)
- JS sandbox hardened: `Function` global frozen alongside `eval` and `Function.prototype.constructor`
- `ScriptedAlgorithm.cpp` reduced from 730→497 lines via `ScriptedAlgorithmHelpers` extraction
- `SplitTree.cpp` serialization extracted to `SplitTreeSerializer.cpp`
- `TilingState.cpp` reduced from 793→500 lines via `TilingStateSerialization.cpp` extraction
- `forEachTiledWindow()` DRY helper eliminates 6+ copies of skip-floating iteration
- Half-null-child guards added to all tree traversals
- Const overloads for `findLeaf`/`leafAtIndex`/`rightmostLeaf`
- `jsArrayToRects` validates `elem.isObject()` before property extraction
- Consistent `count <= 0` guards across all 9 JS algorithms
- Deterministic test assertions (`QCOMPARE` replaces `QVERIFY(>= N)`)
- Data-driven example algorithm smoke tests
- `subtreeHeight`/`treeHeight` renamed from misleading `nodeDepth`/`treeDepth`

## Stats
- **110 files changed**, 6,131 insertions, 1,725 deletions
- **25 new files** (9 algorithms, SplitTree, ScriptedAlgorithm, ScriptedAlgorithmLoader, ScriptedAlgorithmHelpers, SplitTreeSerializer, TilingStateSerialization, DwindleMemoryAlgorithm, 3 test files)
- **56 tests passing**

## Test plan
- [x] 56/56 unit tests pass
- [x] Full build clean (plasmazones_core, plasmazonesd, all test targets)
- [ ] Manual: drop a `.js` in `~/.local/share/plasmazones/algorithms/`, verify it appears under "Custom" section
- [ ] Manual: modify the script, verify KCM updates without restart
- [ ] Manual: delete the script, verify it disappears
- [ ] Manual: select "Dwindle (Memory)", open 3 windows, resize a split, close middle window — verify other splits preserved
- [ ] Manual: verify snapping layout aspect-ratio sections still display correctly
- [ ] Manual: verify all 9 bundled algorithms produce correct previews
- [ ] Manual: switch algorithms, verify per-algorithm split ratio and master count are preserved

author: erickosanchezj
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent Firestore write-batch failures when pruning many invalid FCM tokens across users.  
- Restore paginated user listing to include users that lack a `displayName` field.  
- Avoid clearing the visible users panel before confirming the next-page query succeeded to prevent blank pages on edge cases.

### Description
- Split `pruneMultipleTokensInUsers` into chunked commits using a `MAX_BATCH_WRITES = 500` window and commit each chunk as it fills to avoid exceeding Firestore batch limits, while counting pruned documents. (functions/lib/pruneTokenInUsers.js)  
- Iterate `snap.docs` and track `pendingWrites` to commit each batch when it reaches 500, and commit any remaining writes at the end. (functions/lib/pruneTokenInUsers.js)  
- Change the admin users pagination query to order by `firebase.firestore.FieldPath.documentId()` instead of `displayName` so documents without `displayName` are included in the default paginated list. (admin.html)  
- Delay clearing the current user list UI until after a non-empty page result is received so the current page remains visible when the next-page request returns empty. (admin.html)

### Testing
- Performed a JavaScript syntax check with `node --check functions/lib/pruneTokenInUsers.js` which completed successfully.  
- Verified the diffs of modified files to ensure intended changes were applied (local validation steps).

author: yagobrandalise
body:
## Summary
- Adds a new NPC rewards pipeline with reusable reward actions, multi-task kill support, and profile wiring for reward-driven dialogues.
- Fixes task-kill update concurrency scope in combat flow and resolves nullable inventory/world state handling issues.
- Improves client-side NPC/render behavior and updates dev map assets (`dev2.otbm` + `dev2-spawn.xml`) used by the C# world content flow.
## What changed
### NPC modules and rewards
- Introduced `RewardModule` and reward execution infrastructure:
  - `NpcRewardAction`, `NpcRewardActionType`, `NpcRewardOffer`
  - `RewardActionExecutor`
- Added `MultiTaskKillModule` support for handling multiple kill-task progressions.
- Added `PlayerStorageRequirement` to gate dialogue/reward logic based on player storage state.
- Updated NPC module context/service integration to support the new reward flow.
### NPC profile updates
- Expanded profile providers to use reward/task capabilities:
  - `ProfessorOakNpcProfileProvider`
  - `RewarderNpcProfileProvider`
  - Updates in `Yugo`, `Biro`, `Mark`, `Nurse` providers
- Adjusted greeting/farewell/task module behavior for the new module pipeline.
- Added/updated NPC data file:
  - `server-csharp/src/app/data/npc/Professor Oak.xml`
### Combat and realtime fixes
- Refined lock scope in kill-task updates inside `CombatLoopService` to avoid broader contention.
- Fixed nullable flow warnings/handling in:
  - `RealtimeInventoryState`
  - `RealtimeWorldState`
- Added coverage in `RealtimeInventoryStateTests`.
### Client/runtime fixes
- Updated rendering behavior and tests:
  - `entityRenderer` + click-box test
  - `outfitSprites` + test
- Improved NPC dialog socket routing and added `socketMessageRouter.npcDialog.test.ts`.
### Map/content artifacts
- Added/updated map assets:
  - `server-csharp/src/app/data/map/dev2.otbm`
  - `server-csharp/src/app/data/map/dev2-spawn.xml`
- Updated sample player state fixtures under `server-csharp/src/app/data/players/`.
## Tests
- Added/updated unit/integration tests for:
  - NPC reward modules
  - NPC requirement checks
  - Multi-task kill flow
  - Task kill flow
  - Client NPC dialog routing/render behaviors
  - Realtime inventory nullability paths

## Summary
- add engine-owned FFN/attention parallelism plumbing for training and forward-only benchmarking, including sharded FFN forward/backward and attention-sharded backward paths
- expand correctness and timing coverage with sharded forward/backward harnesses, combined forward checks, and large-scale forward-only probes up to 120B
- switch the workspace `ane` dependency to `https://github.com/ncdrone/ane`, update the bench-result queue / submit flow, and reorganize supporting docs under `docs/`

## Benchmarks
- training sweep `sweep_600m_a`: `1060 ms/step`, `483 tok/s`

body:
## Problem

`SUPERFORECASTER_SHARED_INSTRUCTIONS` contained three near-identical bullets all instructing the model to state Bayesian adjustments with supporting evidence:
- "For each adjustment to the base rate...explicitly state the bayesian adjustment and state the supporting evidence"
- "Explicitly label and make explicit, justified bayesian adjustments for cognitive and source biases"
- "For each adjustment to the confidence value, explicitly state the bayesian adjustment and state the supporting evidence"

Also removed the arbitrary 10-percentage-point check ("could evidence shift my estimate by more than 10 points?"), which is already covered by the sensitivity analysis instruction.

## Change

Merge the three bullets into one: "For each adjustment — to the base rate, for cognitive/source biases, or to confidence — explicitly state the direction, magnitude, supporting evidence, and reasoning."

Also fixes "percentiles" → "confidence intervals" in the uncertainty expression bullet to avoid collision with the `<percentiles>` XML output format for numeric questions.

💡 What: Consolidated 7 individual `.count()` database queries into a single `.aggregate()` query using `Count` and `Q` objects in the `MaintenanceRequestViewSet.stats` action.

🎯 Why: To reduce the number of database roundtrips required to compute dashboard statistics. Performing multiple sequential `.count()` queries on the same table is inefficient and unnecessarily taxes the database connection.

📊 Impact: Reduces the number of database queries from 7 to 1 when calling the `/api/maintenance/stats/` endpoint, decreasing overall latency and server load.

🔬 Measurement: Verified by measuring SQL query execution counts using Django's `connection.queries` in a test script. The original code executed 7 queries, while the new approach executes only 1. Checked via Django shell to ensure correct operation.

author: prashanthreddy064
body:
…her features

Root causes of R²=0.86 and fixes:

1. Multi-task loss competition — brand/zone losses were dragging down units R² Fix: Phase 1 weights units 3x (3.0 vs 0.2), Phase 2 weights units 5x (5.0 vs 0.05)

2. MSE loss sensitive to outliers — a few bad predictions tank R² Fix: Custom Huber loss (delta=0.5) — quadratic for small errors, linear for large

3. Missing the most predictive features Fix: Added 5 new high-power features per timestep:
   - Same-hour-of-day historical average (typical volume at this hour)
   - Same-day-of-week+hour average (most predictive: typical volume for this day+hour)
   - Ratio to hour average (relative strength signal >1 means above normal)
   - Log-transformed units (handles skewed distributions)
   - Previous day lag ratio (yesterday's trend signal)

4. Model not converging fully Fix: Two-phase training:
   - Phase 1: Joint training all outputs, LR=0.001 with reduce-on-plateau
   - Phase 2: Freeze conv layers, fine-tune only dense/units head at LR=0.0002

5. Dropout too aggressive at 0.15 Fix: Reduced to 0.05 across all layers

6. Architecture: Added 5th conv block with residual, skip connection from pooling directly to units head for better gradient flow

body:
Gallery images loaded from hardcoded HTML were producing inconsistent row heights on desktop due to unconstrained image containers. Images are now served from a dedicated `imgs/` folder and rendered dynamically from a JSON manifest.

## Changes

### New files
- **`imgs/`** — all gallery images copied from `Unga/` (JPG + WebP variants, srcset sizes preserved)
- **`imgs/gallery.json`** — 10-item manifest: image paths, WebP srcsets, `alt_it`/`alt_en`, grid span/size classes, `i18n` keys
- **`gallery.js`** — IIFE; fetches `/imgs/gallery.json`, renders identical `<figure><picture><figcaption>` markup, calls existing `setLang()` for translations, wires new `IntersectionObserver` with DOM-order stagger

```json
{
  "src": "/imgs/VogueSposa.JPG",
  "webp_srcset": "/imgs/VogueSposa-640.webp 640w, /imgs/VogueSposa.webp 1066w",
  "sizes": "(max-width: 860px) 100vw, 50vw",
  "span": "span-6", "size": "tall",
  "loading": "eager", "fetchpriority": "high",
  "i18n_title": "port_1_title", "i18n_desc": "port_1_desc",
  "alt_it": "...", "alt_en": "..."
}
```

### `index.html` / `en/index.html`
- Portfolio grid body replaced with `<div class="portfolio-grid" id="gallery-grid">` (empty; populated by `gallery.js`)
- `<link rel="preload">` updated from `Unga/` → `/imgs/`
- `<script src="/gallery.js" defer>` added before `</body>`

### CSS (both pages)
- `picture { display:block; width:100%; height:100%; }` — ensures image fills container for `object-fit:cover` to work
- `.tall/.med/.small`: `min-height` → fixed `height` (520/420/320px) — eliminates variable row heights on desktop; mobile override updated to match

### Notes
- `Unga/` folder retained; OG/Twitter meta images still reference it
- To add a gallery item: drop image into `imgs/`, append one JSON entry — no HTML edits needed

author: guyb1
body:
## Summary

Credentials added via the dashboard were not immediately available to agents due to the gateway's 60-second CONNECT response cache. This adds cache invalidation so changes take effect instantly.

## Changes

**Gateway (Rust):**
- Add `del_by_prefix` method to `CacheStore` trait (both InMemory and Redis implementations)
- Include `account_id` in cache key format: `connect:{account_id}:{token}:{host}`
- Add `POST /api/cache/invalidate` endpoint (authenticated, scoped to caller's account)

**Web app (TypeScript):**
- Add `useInvalidateGatewayCache` hook for client-side cache busting
- Call it after every secret create/update/delete, rule create/update/delete/toggle, agent token regeneration, agent deletion, and agent secret assignment changes

## How it works

1. User mutates a secret/rule/agent in the dashboard
2. Server action saves to DB
3. Client fires `POST /api/cache/invalidate` to the gateway (fire-and-forget)
4. Gateway clears all cached CONNECT responses for that account
5. Next agent request hits the DB and gets fresh data

Fixes #116

author: copilot
body:
# Description

This pull request updates the regex in the maintain-pr-description workflow to ensure that the entire Description section is captured, rather than just the first line. The changes in the YAML file adjust the regex pattern to accommodate multiline descriptions, enhancing the accuracy of PR descriptions.

<!-- description-auto-generated-by-copilot -->




With the `m` (multiline) flag active, `$` in `(?=\n#{1,3}\s|$)` matches at the end of every line — not just end-of-string. The non-greedy `[\s\S]*?` therefore stops at the first line break after `# Description`, so only line 1 of any multi-line auto-generated description is captured on re-generation. Subsequent `synchronize` runs leave stale old lines accumulating inside the Description section after the auto-marker.

## Changes

- **`getDescriptionSectionContent` regex** — replaced `$` with `(?![\s\S])` so the detection captures the full section content (all lines up to the next `#` heading or end-of-string)
- **Replacement regex** — same fix applied so re-generation replaces the entire prior description rather than just its first line

```diff
- const sectionRegex = /^#{1,3}\s+Description\s*\n([\s\S]*?)(?=\n#{1,3}\s|$)/m;
+ const sectionRegex = /^#{1,3}\s+Description\s*\n([\s\S]*?)(?=\n#{1,3}\s|(?![\s\S]))/m;
```

`(?![\s\S])` is a zero-width negative lookahead that matches only at true end-of-string regardless of the `m` flag, while `\n#{1,3}\s` still handles the normal case of a following section heading.

author: mvanhorn
body:
## Summary

Adds language detection to Phase 1 Setup and provides per-language variants for approach hints 3, 4, 6, and 7. Supports Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, and a generic fallback.

## Why this matters

The skill positions itself as language-agnostic ("An open-source agent skill for Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI"), but all 10 approach hints contain Python-specific constructs. Hint 4 tells a Go implementer to "make the interface Pythonic with `with` statements" and reference `__enter__`. Hint 3 suggests `dataclasses` and `named tuples`. Hint 6 references `asyncio`. Hint 7 suggests `@rate_limit` decorator syntax.

When the skill runs on a TypeScript, Go, or Rust project, these hints are confusing. The implementer either ignores the hint (wasting a diversity slot) or awkwardly adapts it (producing worse code).

## Changes

- Added language detection step (step 5) to Phase 1 Setup in `SKILL.md` using file extension analysis
- Replaced hardcoded Python hints 3, 4, 6, 7 with per-language variant tables
- Each table covers: Python (unchanged), TypeScript, Go, Rust, generic fallback
- Language-neutral hints (1, 2, 5, 8, 9, 10) stay identical
- Updated contract test keyword list in `test-contracts.sh` to include TypeScript/Go/Rust architectural terms (goroutine, channel, trait, Promise, AbortController, middleware, builder, Iterator, tokio, etc.)

## Video Demo

![Demo](https://files.catbox.moe/exenx4.gif)

## Testing

- `./tests/run-tests.sh` passes (all contract and structure tests)
- Contract 7 validates 41 distinct architectural keywords across all language variants (needs >= 4)
- All template variables remain documented in SKILL.md

author: lf-itx-dev
body:
Add new CI please!
# CI/CD on github-actions

This pull request adds The Linux Foundation docker
toolchain for CI/CD workflows on github-actions.

## Toolchain

The CI/CD workflows for this repository are triggered by the following:

* Pull Requests: pull requests against main will verify the project
  container can be built. The container won't be pushed anywhere.
* Merge: Merges to the repository build the docker container and tag it
  with ':latest', and 
  push it to github-packages. 
* Release: On tags, the container is built, tagged with both the
  specified tag and ':latest' and pushed to github-packages.


## Docker Environment Variables

The following variables are available to workflows:
- `$DOCKER_IMAGE`
  Name of the docker image to create
- `$DOCKER_BUILDCONTEXT`
  Path to the build context for the docker image
- `$DOCKER_FILEPATH`
  Path to the Dockerfile being built
- `$DOCKER_REPOSITORY`
  Name of the docker registry repository where the image will be
  distributed


## Updating this Pull Request

If these workflows don't match the needs for your project feel free to
[modify](https://help.github.com/en/github/collaborating-with-issues-and-pull-requests/checking-out-pull-requests-locally) them to meet your needs.

body:
### Motivation
- The on-canvas Celdra sprite was visually off-center and the sprite-sheet contained a baked checkerboard background that should be treated as transparent at render time.
- Keep the current canvas-based player and existing state/bubble behavior while making placement and masking tunable for later adjustments.
- Provide convenient top-level tuning knobs so artists or devs can quickly adjust scale and masking thresholds without digging into rendering code.

### Description
- Added top-level tuning constants `DRAW_SCALE`, `DRAW_OFFSET_X`, `DRAW_OFFSET_Y`, `STATE_OFFSETS`, `MASK_BRIGHTNESS_MIN`, `MASK_NEUTRAL_TOLERANCE`, and `MASK_ALPHA` to `celdra-corner.js` for placement and masking configuration.
- Updated the draw path to compute an aspect-ratio-preserving `finalScale` and center the sprite in the canvas while applying global and per-state offsets and a small downward default offset.
- Implemented offscreen per-frame preprocessing that copies the cropped frame into an offscreen canvas, iterates pixels to reduce alpha for bright neutral (checkerboard) pixels using the tunable thresholds, writes the processed `ImageData` back, and caches processed frames for reuse.
- Preserved the existing state system and timelines and extended `ANIMS` to include `sleepy` and `excited` entries while keeping `idle`, `blink`, and `sleep` behavior intact, and added a small guard to fall back if an offscreen context is unavailable.

### Testing
- Ran static validation with `node --check celdra-corner.js`, which completed successfully with no syntax errors.
- No other automated browser rendering tests were available in this environment.

## Summary

- **Self-healing cookie flow**: When no node cookie is configured, `beam_agent_credential` now generates a cryptographically secure ephemeral cookie (32 bytes / 256 bits, URL-safe base64), applies it to the running node via `erlang:set_cookie/2`, derives the AES-256-GCM encryption key, and logs a warning with persistence instructions — instead of crashing.
- **No secrets in logs**: The logger warning tells the user to call `erlang:get_cookie()` / `Node.get_cookie()` to retrieve the cookie value. The cookie itself is never logged.
- **Dead code removed**: All ~35 `{error, nocookie}` / `{error, {credential_unavailable, nocookie}}` error propagation paths in `runtime_core`, `runtime`, `provider`, and `command` modules reverted — they were unreachable after auto-generation.

author: dkruenbo
body:
## Summary

Two small fixes for guild chat messaging, released as 1.3.2.

### Fix 1 — Guild chat message truncation (`[>]` post button)

`FormatCraftersLine` budgets `255 - prefixLen - 15` bytes for its crafter list. `PostCraftersToGuildChat` then appends ` — /gc to browse` (18 bytes, including the 3-byte UTF-8 em dash) **after** calling `FormatCraftersLine`. Combined, the message could reach 258 bytes — WoW silently truncates at 255, cutting the last 3 bytes of the trailer on recipes with many crafters.

**Fix:** `FormatCraftersLine` now accepts an optional `extraReserve` parameter (defaults to `0`, so all other call sites are unchanged). `PostCraftersToGuildChat` passes `#BROWSE_SUFFIX` (18) so the budget correctly accounts for the trailer.

### Fix 2 — `!gc` overflow line display

When a `!gc` query matched more than 3 recipes, the overflow notice rendered as:
```
[GuildCrafts] ...3 more result(s)
```
(the count ran directly into the ellipsis with no space)

**Fix:** Changed to:
```
[GuildCrafts] +3 more result(s) — /gc to browse
```

## Risk

Low. Fix 1's `extraReserve` defaults to `0` — all call sites that don't pass it are byte-for-byte identical to before. Fix 2 is a pure display string change on an infrequently hit code path.

author: ivangegovdve-sudo
body:
💡 What
Wrapped the main content of `src/app/browse/page.tsx` (`BrowseContent`) inside a React `<Suspense>` boundary using the existing `BrowseSkeleton` component as a fallback.

🎯 Why
Next.js was statically rendering the `/browse` route, but encountering the `useSearchParams()` hook inside the component without a Suspense boundary caused the entire route to bail out of static rendering and de-opt to full client-side rendering (CSR bailout). This prevents the page shell from being statically generated at build time.

📊 Impact
Enabling static generation of the page shell dramatically reduces Time to First Byte (TTFB). Typical Server-Side Rendering (SSR) times can take ~100-300ms or more depending on database and API load, while statically generated page shells delivered from a CDN edge take roughly ~10-50ms.

🔬 Measurement
Run `npm run build` and observe that the Next.js build output for the `/browse` route no longer throws the `useSearchParams() should be wrapped in a suspense boundary` error. The route will now correctly be pre-rendered as a static shell with client-side data fetching.

author: navarrs
body:
This pull request introduces support for the final sample-selection strategy called Den-TP based on this recent [paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.17385). Code for the original implementation is not available, but we implement the core idea with a core modification that uses model embeddings instead of gradients. 

**Main Updates:**

**Den-TP strategy integration:**

* Added Den-TP (`den_tp`) as a valid sample selection type and strategy in `run_sample_selection_sweep.sh`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2a1311b4da24c16e9bd4abe13e514900af380de11b26817aec0b60252c9f5ea4L17-R21) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2a1311b4da24c16e9bd4abe13e514900af380de11b26817aec0b60252c9f5ea4R79-R81) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2a1311b4da24c16e9bd4abe13e514900af380de11b26817aec0b60252c9f5ea4R133-R137)
* Updated configuration file `sample_selection.yaml` to include `den_tp` as a selectable strategy, added Den-TP-specific parameters (`density_interval`), and clarified documentation for Den-TP usage. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b43b8fb84214c8f11639ae6f7ac794810517e2d4756acebc971d1521164c6fefR22) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b43b8fb84214c8f11639ae6f7ac794810517e2d4756acebc971d1521164c6fefR35-R42) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b43b8fb84214c8f11639ae6f7ac794810517e2d4756acebc971d1521164c6fefL62-R68)
* Added `DEN_TP` to the `SampleSelection` enum. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c9da64dcc1b571801aa988fc05f2cb7c7e33969fa92ab087622af392e4a8ec4aR9)

**Algorithm implementation:**

* Implemented the Den-TP algorithm in `sample_selection_utils.py`, including functions for density binning, greedy submodular selection, and partitioned budget allocation. The main entry point is `dentp_selection`, which is now invoked when the Den-TP strategy is selected. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-00a8c76f009ae09ac15d0a04b5270de22f0cc5dadb163e77ddbd8fbc67e191a2L16-R17) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-00a8c76f009ae09ac15d0a04b5270de22f0cc5dadb163e77ddbd8fbc67e191a2R430-R554) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-00a8c76f009ae09ac15d0a04b5270de22f0cc5dadb163e77ddbd8fbc67e191a2R595-R596)
* Added a utility function `compute_pairwise_cosine_similarity` in `metric_utils.py` to compute pairwise similarities required by Den-TP.


**NOTE:** In the future, we can refactor the `sample_selection_utils.py` file so that it becomes a module in the project.

### Motivation
- Make the live platform self-monitoring so it can automatically identify model deterioration, operational issues, and data-source problems using transparent, configurable checks.
- Detect key signals including CLV deterioration, value-flag hit-rate drops, benchmark coverage/missingness, calibration degradation, abnormal value volume, league/market concentration, stale snapshots, and failed/partial runs using rolling windows vs historical baselines.
- Persist alerts in an audit-friendly, append-only form and surface serious issues via the existing notification path while exposing open/current and historical alert views in the dashboard.

### Description
- Added a typed `DriftAlertConfig` to `AppConfig` and added `drift_alerts` thresholds to `config/runtime.yaml` to make windows and thresholds configurable via `DriftAlertConfig` and `cfg.drift_alerts`.
- Implemented `detect_drift_alerts`, `build_open_alerts`, and `build_email_alert_events` in `src/footballmodel/live/monitoring.py` to compute rolling-window stats and produce alert records with audit fields (id, timestamp, type, severity, config/version, market/league, metric, observed/baseline/delta, window, status, details).
- Wired alert generation into the live run flow in `scripts/run_pipeline.py`, appending to `live_alert_history`, writing `live_open_alerts`, and appending queued notification rows to `live_alert_notifications_history` for severe alerts.
- Extended the Run Control UI (`app/pages/Run_Control.py`) to show current open alerts, alert counts by severity/type, affected markets/leagues, and full alert history; updated the dashboard fake repo and smoke tests to load the new tables.

### Testing
- Added unit tests for drift detection and severe-notification selection (`tests/test_live_monitoring.py`) and updated dashboard smoke fixtures (`tests/test_dashboard_smoke.py`).
- Ran the test suite with `pytest -q` and all tests passed: 52 passed (4 warnings).

author: nongjossss-commits
body:
This pull request addresses the user's request to properly synchronize an employee's state when they are deleted or transferred between employers.

**Changes:**
1. **Deletion Sync:** When an employee is deleted from the main database, the system checks if they are active in any sub-menus (Registration, Renewal, Workflow) and asks if the user wants to cancel those operations too.
2. **Sub-Menu Deletion:** When an employee is removed from a sub-menu, the system asks if the user wants to soft-delete them from the main database as well. If they choose no, the employee simply gets a `cancelled` status in that menu. If they choose yes, the employee is fully soft-deleted but retains visibility in the menu with a red badge indicating they are in the trash.
3. **Employer Transfer:** When transferring an employee (singly or in bulk), the system checks for active workflows with the old employer and offers three choices:
   - Keep: Leave the workflow assigned to the old employer.
   - Move: Recreate the workflow (Production Order) for the new employer and move the item.
   - Cancel: Cancel the active workflow.

author: jagarcell
body:
## Summary

Introduces typed PHP enums for game status and user roles, replacing all bare string literals across the service and repository layers. All mutation routes and sensitive listing endpoints are moved behind `auth:sanctum` + `throttle:api` middleware and backed by a named rate-limiter. A migration adds previously missing database indexes, and the frontend components are decomposed into focused sub-components backed by a shared API client and utility modules.

## Changes

### Backend
- `**feat:**` `app/Enums/GameStatus.php`, `app/Enums/GameUserRole.php` — Add two backed string enums (`GameStatus`, `GameUserRole`) to centralise all status and role constants.
- `**refactor:**` `app/Models/Game.php`, `app/Repositories/BurakoGameRepository.php`, `app/Services/BurakoGameService.php` — Cast `Game::$status` to `GameStatus`; replace every bare `'in_progress'`, `'finished'`, `'creator'`, `'pending_invitee'`, and `'viewer'` literal with their enum counterparts; add `lockForUpdate()` to `getNextRoundNumber()` to prevent concurrent duplicate round numbers.
- `**security:**` `routes/api.php`, `app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php` — Move `GET /v1/users`, `GET /v1/teams`, and all write routes into `['auth:sanctum', 'throttle:api']`; register the named `api` rate-limiter (60 req/min per user ID, IP fallback).
- `**fix:**` `database/migrations/2026_03_26_000000_add_missing_indexes.php` — Add indexes on columns used in `WHERE`/`JOIN`/`ORDER BY` clauses that were previously unindexed.
- `**fix:**` `bootstrap/app.php` — Register a JSON renderable for `ValidationException` that wraps errors in the standard envelope (`status`, `data.message`, `data.errors`, `http_code: 422`).

### Frontend
- `**feat:**` `resources/js/api/client.js`, `resources/js/utils/formatGameName.js`, `resources/js/utils/strings.js` — Introduce a shared Axios-based API client and two utility modules (game-name formatting, string helpers) to remove ad-hoc logic from components.
- `**refactor:**` `resources/js/Pages/Dashboard.jsx`, `resources/js/Components/GameCard.jsx`, `resources/js/Components/RoundsCard.jsx`, `resources/js/Components/TeamsCard.jsx` — Decompose large components into focused sub-components; migrate to the shared API client and utilities.

### Tests
- `**test:**` `tests/Feature/Api/GameUpdateTest.php`, `PlayerSeatSwapTest.php`, `RoundDraftTest.php`, `ScorePersistenceTest.php`, `TeamIndexTest.php`, `TeamPlayerDestroyTest.php`, `TeamPlayerStoreTest.php`, `TeamStoreTest.php`, `TeamUpdateTest.php`, `UserIndexTest.php` — Add `setUp()` with `actingAs()` to all feature test classes calling routes now behind `auth:sanctum`; restores the full 248-test green suite.
- `**refactor:**` `resources/js/Components/__tests__/GameCard.test.jsx`, `RoundsCard.test.jsx`, `TeamsCard.test.jsx` — Update component tests to match new sub-component structure and API client usage.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `app/Enums/GameStatus.php` | New — backed string enum for game status values |
| `app/Enums/GameUserRole.php` | New — backed string enum for game user role values |
| `app/Models/Game.php` | Modified — add `$casts` for `status → GameStatus` |
| `app/Repositories/BurakoGameRepository.php` | Modified — replace bare string literals with enums; add `lockForUpdate()` |
| `app/Services/BurakoGameService.php` | Modified — replace bare string literals with enums |
| `routes/api.php` | Modified — move mutation + listing routes into `auth:sanctum` + `throttle:api` group |
| `app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php` | Modified — register named `api` rate-limiter |
| `database/migrations/2026_03_26_000000_add_missing_indexes.php` | New — add missing column indexes |
| `bootstrap/app.php` | Modified — add `ValidationException` JSON envelope renderable |
| `resources/js/api/client.js` | New — shared Axios API client |
| `resources/js/utils/formatGameName.js` | New — game name formatting utility |
| `resources/js/utils/strings.js` | New — general string helpers |
| `resources/js/Pages/Dashboard.jsx` | Modified — decomposed into sub-components; uses API client |
| `resources/js/Components/GameCard.jsx` | Modified — focused sub-components; uses utilities |
| `resources/js/Components/RoundsCard.jsx` | Modified — focused sub-components; uses utilities |
| `resources/js/Components/TeamsCard.jsx` | Modified — focused sub-components; uses utilities |
| `resources/js/Components/__tests__/GameCard.test.jsx` | Modified — updated for new component structure |
| `resources/js/Components/__tests__/RoundsCard.test.jsx` | Modified — updated for new component structure |
| `resources/js/Components/__tests__/TeamsCard.test.jsx` | Modified — updated for new component structure |
| `tests/Feature/Api/GameUpdateTest.php` | Modified — add `setUp` + `actingAs` |
| `tests/Feature/Api/PlayerSeatSwapTest.php` | Modified — add `setUp` + `actingAs` |
| `tests/Feature/Api/RoundDraftTest.php` | Modified — add `actingAs` to existing `setUp` |
| `tests/Feature/Api/ScorePersistenceTest.php` | Modified — add `actingAs` to existing `setUp` |
| `tests/Feature/Api/TeamIndexTest.php` | Modified — add `setUp` + `actingAs` |
| `tests/Feature/Api/TeamPlayerDestroyTest.php` | Modified — add `setUp` + `actingAs` |
| `tests/Feature/Api/TeamPlayerStoreTest.php` | Modified — add `setUp` + `actingAs` |
| `tests/Feature/Api/TeamStoreTest.php` | Modified — add `setUp` + `actingAs` |
| `tests/Feature/Api/TeamUpdateTest.php` | Modified — add `setUp` + `actingAs` |
| `tests/Feature/Api/UserIndexTest.php` | Modified — add `setUp` + `actingAs` using `make()` |

## QA Steps

1. **Setup:** copy `.env.example` to `.env`, run `php artisan key:generate`, configure a local DB, then run `php artisan migrate`.
2. **Run PHP test suite:** `php artisan test --no-coverage` — all 248 tests must pass with 765 assertions.
3. **Verify unauthenticated mutation is blocked:** send `POST /api/v1/games` without an auth token and assert a `401` response.
4. **Verify unauthenticated listing is blocked:** send `GET /api/v1/users` and `GET /api/v1/teams` without a token and assert `401`.
5. **Verify unauthenticated public routes still work:** send `GET /api/v1/health`, `GET /api/v1/games/{id}`, `GET /api/v1/base-elements` without a token and assert `200`.
6. **Verify enum cast:** fetch an in-progress game via `GET /api/v1/games/{id}` (authenticated) and confirm `status` in the response is `"in_progress"`.
7. **Verify ValidationException envelope:** send an invalid `POST /api/v1/games` payload (authenticated) and assert the response has shape `{ status: "error", data: { message: "...", errors: {...} }, http_code: 422 }`.
8. **Verify rate-limiter:** with a valid token, send 61 requests to any mutation route within one minute and assert the 61st returns `429`.
9. **Run migrations on a clean DB** and confirm all indexes are created without errors.
10. **Frontend smoke test:** run `npm run build` without errors; open the dashboard, verify game cards render correctly, teams and rounds cards display their data, and the UI is responsive on a mobile viewport (≤ 375 px).

When SPI health check fails, read the CC1101 PARTNUM and VERSION status

- Unexpected chip ID (wrong SPI bus or not a CC1101)

author: rohansiyer
body:
## Summary

- Adds a `ripple_field` Numba `@njit` function computing the N_TF-fold toroidal ripple perturbation: `δ(r,φ) = δ_max·cos(N_TF·φ)·exp(-N_TF·(r/R₀)^N_TF)`
- Modifies `_gc_derivatives` to apply ripple to: (1) local |B| for μ-conservation, (2) ∇B drift via the ripple-modified field magnitude, and (3) the parallel mirror force via `∂B/∂φ|_ripple`, enabling ripple trapping for particles with `|v_par/v_perp| < √δ`
- Adds `N_TF=18` and `ripple_amplitude=0.001` keyword arguments to both `_gc_derivatives` and `pic_push_particles` — existing call sites without these kwargs continue to work unchanged
- Updates `__main__.py` to forward `N_TF=cfg.N_TF, ripple_amplitude=0.001` to `pic_push_particles`

## Physics background

Real tokamaks have N_TF discrete TF coils that break toroidal symmetry and produce a small ripple in |B|. At ITER-like parameters (N_TF=18, r/R₀~0.3), δ_max~0.1%. This ripple:
- Modifies v_perp through μ conservation at the local field
- Creates ripple-trapped particle orbits (banana-like but between adjacent coils)
- Causes ripple-induced transport, a known loss channel for fast ions

The perturbation is < 0.1% of B₀ and is numerically stable.

## Test plan

- [x] All 41 existing physics tests pass without modification
- [x] `ripple_field` verified to return `|δ| < 0.001` at ITER mid-radius
- [x] `pic_push_particles` signature confirmed backward-compatible (default kwargs)
- [x] Module imports cleanly; Numba `@njit` compilation succeeds

closes #131 

Summary

This PR resolves stale cache reads occurring after transaction status updates by ensuring immediate cache invalidation within the same execution flow as the database mutation.

Previously, updated transaction statuses could remain outdated in cache until TTL expiration, leading to inconsistent reads immediately after a write.

Changes Made
Added targeted cache invalidation logic in the transaction update flow (post-commit)
Ensured invalidation occurs within the same logical operation as the database update
Preserved existing cache TTL behavior for unaffected records
Avoided broad cache clears by invalidating only specific transaction-related keys
Introduced a fallback mechanism to detect potential stale reads via metrics/logging
Added tests to verify:
Cache invalidation on status update
Immediate read consistency after mutation

author: ajjimeno
body:
## Summary
Add Tensorlake Firecracker microVM sandbox as an opt-in backend for shell command execution, isolating all LLM-issued shell calls from the host machine.

## Context
Forge currently executes every shell tool call directly on the user's host machine. For agentic workflows this creates risk: a misguided or adversarial command runs with the user's full OS permissions. Tensorlake provides Firecracker microVM sandboxes that boot in sub-second time, persist filesystem state across commands within a session, and auto-suspend on inactivity — making them a natural fit for containing Forge's shell execution without sacrificing the stateful environment agents rely on.

## Changes
- **`TensorlakeCommandExecutor`** (`crates/forge_infra/src/tensorlake.rs`): new `CommandInfra` implementation that provisions a Tensorlake sandbox lazily on the first command, reuses it for the entire session, and terminates it on drop via a best-effort background task.
- **`ForgeInfra`** (`crates/forge_infra/src/forge_infra.rs`): introduces a `CommandExecutor` enum (`Local` | `Tensorlake`) and a new `ForgeInfra::new_with_tensorlake()` constructor; all existing `CommandInfra` delegation is unchanged.
- **`forge_infra/src/lib.rs`**: exports the `tensorlake` module and re-exports `TensorlakeConfig`.
- **`ForgeAPI`** (`crates/forge_api/src/forge_api.rs`): adds `ForgeAPI::init_with_tensorlake()` factory that mirrors `init()` but selects the Tensorlake executor.
- **`forge_api/src/lib.rs`**: re-exports `TensorlakeConfig` so callers don't need to import `forge_infra` directly.
- **CLI** (`crates/forge_main/src/cli.rs` + `main.rs`): adds `--tensorlake <API_KEY>` flag (also reads `TENSORLAKE_API_KEY` env var); when provided, `init_with_tensorlake()` is used instead of `init()`.

### Key Implementation Details
- The sandbox ID is stored in `Arc<Mutex<Option<String>>>` so clones of the executor share the same lazily-provisioned sandbox.
- `execute_command_raw` (used for interactive/TTY commands) returns an explicit error in Tensorlake mode — raw stdin cannot be forwarded over HTTP.
- Sandbox cleanup is best-effort: a `tokio::spawn` is fired from `Drop` to call `DELETE /v2/sandboxes/{id}` without blocking the caller.
- No changes to domain, services, or tool executor layers — the integration is confined entirely to the infrastructure layer, consistent with the project's clean architecture.

## Use Cases
```bash
# Route all shell commands through a Tensorlake microVM
forge --tensorlake sk-tl-xxxx

# Or via environment variable
TENSORLAKE_API_KEY=sk-tl-xxxx forge
```

## Testing
```bash
# Verify forge_infra compiles cleanly
cargo check -p forge_infra

# Run unit tests for the new executor
cargo test -p forge_infra tensorlake

# End-to-end: set a real API key and run a shell-heavy task
TENSORLAKE_API_KEY=<key> forge --prompt "list files in /tmp"
```

## Links
- Tensorlake sandbox docs: https://docs.tensorlake.ai/sandboxes/introduction
- Tensorlake Python SDK: `pip install tensorlake`

## What this PR does
Adds the complete Prisma database layer: schema for Check, Lead, and RateLimit models, a singleton PrismaClient, and typed repository functions for each model.

## Implementation notes
- Singleton pattern for PrismaClient prevents connection pool exhaustion in long-running processes
- Repositories encapsulate all Prisma calls — no other file should import prisma directly
- `checks.repository.findByUrlHash` filters expired records (expiresAt < now) at the query level, not in application code
- Lead creation handles P2002 (unique constraint) gracefully — returns existing record instead of throwing
- RateLimit upsert uses Prisma's upsert with atomic increment via raw SQL update

## How to test
1. `docker-compose up -d` — start Postgres
2. `cp .env.example .env`
3. `npm install && npx prisma migrate dev --name initial`
4. `npm test` — unit tests with mocked Prisma pass without DB
5. To verify against real DB: `npx prisma studio` — check tables exist

- [ ] Unit tests pass (`npm test`)
- [ ] No regressions in existing tests
- [ ] Error cases handled (unique constraint on leads, expired check filtering)
- [ ] Contracts respected (types imported from src/types/index.ts)

author: copilot
body:
The SINCO SMC-PAD Pocket sends absolute CC (0–127) from its knobs by default. To use them as Zynthian zynpots (which expect raw +1/−1 relative CC), the hardware's flash must be updated directly via SysEx rather than translating in software.

## Changes

- **`set_knobs_relative.py`** — iterates all 8 presets × 8 knobs, writes type byte `0x01` (CC Relative) to each knob's flash address, then commits with a save packet
  - Address formula from Ghidra decompile of MidiSuite: `(preset * 0xDD3) + (knob * 6) + 0x73`
  - Full 7-bit MIDI encoding of raw packets per the device's SysEx protocol
  - 50 ms inter-write delay; progress printed per write

- **`verify_knobs.py`** — companion script; sends flash-read (`0x23`) for each address, decodes the 7-bit response, and reports `✓`/`✗` per knob

- **`README.md`** — prerequisites, usage, knob type value table, protocol summary, and Zynthian zynpot wiring notes

## Key protocol details

```
# Raw packet before 7-bit encoding (flash write, 1-byte payload)
[00 59]          # header
[22]             # cmd = flash write
[09 00 00]       # size = data_len + 8, little-endian
[05]             # FlashType = 5
[addr 4 bytes]   # little-endian address
[01 00 00]       # data_len = 1
[01]             # data = CC Relative
[checksum]       # ~sum(bytes[6:]) & 0xFF
```

All 64 knob slots are set (8 presets × 8 knobs) so CC Relative is active regardless of which preset is loaded. A power-cycle is required after writing.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Goal

Write a Python script that uses the SMC-PAD Pocket's SysEx protocol to set **all 8 knobs** (across all 8 presets) to **CC Relative mode** (type byte `0x01`) by writing directly to the device's flash via SysEx.

This is for use with Zynthian, where the top-row knobs will act as zynpots sending raw +1/-1 relative CC data.

---

## Protocol Background (from Ghidra decompilation of MidiSuite)

### SysEx transport
- **Port**: `SINCO SMC-PAD Pocket-Private`
- **Header** (raw before 7-bit encoding): `00 59`
- All SysEx data is **7-bit packed** before sending (every 8 input bytes → 9 output bytes, MSBs collected into a prefix byte)
- **Full SysEx frame**: `F0 [7-bit encoded payload] F7`

### Flash Write command (`0x22`)
Raw packet structure (before 7-bit encoding):
```
Offset  Size  Field
------  ----  -----
0-1     2     Header (00 59)
2       1     Command = 0x22
3-5     3     Size = data_len + 8 (little-endian)
6       1     FlashType = 0x05
7-10    4     Address (little-endian)
11-13   3     Data length (little-endian)
14+     N     Data bytes
Last    1     Checksum = ~(sum of bytes from offset 6 onward, before checksum) & 0xFF
```

### Knob type byte address formula (from decompiled `FUN_100041160`)
```c
flash_addr = (preset * 0xDD3) + (knob_index * 6) + 0x73
```
- `preset`: 0–7 (8 presets total, confirmed by `0x6E98 / 0xDD3 = 8`)
- `knob_index`: 0–7 (8 knobs)
- `FlashType`: 5

### Knob type values (from ComboBox index in MidiSuite UI)
- `0x00` = CC Absolute
- `0x01` = CC Relative  ← **this is what we want**
- `0x02` = Note
- `0x03` = Program Change
- `0x04` = Disabled/SysEx

### Flash Save/Commit command (`0x22` with data_len=0)
Raw packet:
```
Offset  Size  Field
------  ----  -----
0-1     2     Header (00 59)
2       1     Command = 0x22
3-5     3     Size = 8 (fixed, little-endian)
6       1     FlashType = 0x05
7-10    4     Address = 0x00000000
11-13   3     Data length = 0
14      1     Checksum = ~(FlashType + addr_bytes) & 0xFF
```

### 7-bit encoding algorithm
Pack 8-bit bytes into 7-bit MIDI-safe bytes:
- For every group of 7 input bytes, emit 8 output bytes
- First output byte = the MSBs of the 7 input bytes (bit 6 = MSB of byte 0, bit 5 = MSB of byte 1, etc.)
- Remaining 7 output bytes = input bytes with their MSB cleared (& 0x7F)
- If the last group has fewer than 7 bytes, pad accordingly

---

## What to build

### `set_knobs_relative.py`

A self-contained Python 3 script that:

1. **Opens** the `SINCO SMC-PAD Pocket-Private` MIDI port using `mido` + `python-rtmidi`
2. **For each of the 8 presets** (0–7):
   - **For each of the 8 knobs** (0–7):
     - Computes `flash_addr = (preset * 0xDD3) + (knob * 6) + 0x73`
     - Builds the raw flash-write packet (header + cmd + size + flashtype + addr + datalen + data + checksum)
     - 7-bit encodes it
     - Sends it as a SysEx message
     - Waits ~50ms between writes
3. **Sends the flash save/commit** packet after all writes
4. Prints progress as it goes: `Setting preset {p} knob {k} @ flash addr 0x{addr:04X} → 0x01`
5. Prints a final message: `Done. Power-cycle the SMC-PAD to apply changes.`

### `verify_knobs.py`

A companion script that:

1. Opens the same port
2. For each preset/knob, sends a **flash read** (`0x23`) for 1 byte at the same address
3. Decodes the response and prints whether each knob is set to `0x01` (Relative) or something else

### Flash Read command (`0x23`) for verify script
Raw packet:
```
Offset  Size  Field
------  ----  -----
0-1     2     Header (00 59)
2       1     Command = 0x23
3-5     3     Size = 8 (little-endian)
6       1     FlashType = 0x05
7-10    4     Address (little-endian)
11-13   3     Data length (little-endian)
14      1     Checksum = ~(sum of bytes from offset 6) & 0xFF
```
Response length after 7-bit decode: `data_len + 0x0F` bytes.

### `README.md`

Document:
- What this does and why
- Prerequisites: `pip install mido python-rtmidi`
- Usage: `python set_knobs_relative.py` then power-cycle
- How to verify: `python verify_knobs.py`
- The knob type value table
- Warning: power-cycle required for changes to take effect
- Note that this targets all 8 knobs across all 8 presets so every preset has relative knobs


The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated):

User: that doesn't help though since we can set midi CC's. what you are finind is probable custom setups for midisuite

Assistant: You're absolutely right — good catch. Those `MIDI_Map.py` values are **Ableton remote script configurations**, meaning they describe what the *software* is listening for after the user has remapped the device via **Midisuite**. They tell us nothing reliable about what the hardware actually sends by default.

Let me search for raw/default protocol info instead.

Assistant: You're absolutely right — and this is a goldmine. The `malpern/claudepad` repo is **exactly the right kind of source**: it's a reverse-engineering effort on the **SINCO SMC-PAD Pocket** whi...

author: dhruvhaldar
body:
💡 What: Removed a redundant `.clone()` call on the `alert_text` variable when pushing a new `LogEntry::Alert` into the `logs` collection within the parsing error path of `process_result`.
🎯 Why: Because `alert_text` is no longer used in the local scope after insertion, preemptively cloning it forces an entirely unnecessary heap allocation and deep copy. Moving ownership directly is safe and more efficient.
📊 Impact: Eliminates a redundant O(1) string allocation and copy per protocol parsing alert generated, reducing memory churn and GC overhead on hot paths.
🔬 Measurement: Verify by running standard telemetry parsing fuzzing/tests (`cargo test`) to ensure expected logging behavior without the hidden cost of redundant allocations. Added a learning to `.jules/bolt.md`.

body:
## Problem

The migration file `backend/prisma/migrations/20260314220000_sync_schema_to_latest/migration.sql` used single `$` as the dollar-quote delimiter for its `DO` block (`DO $ BEGIN ... END $;`), which is invalid PostgreSQL syntax and causes a "syntax error at or near "$"" error when the migration runs.

## Solution

Replaced the single `$` delimiters with the required double dollar-sign form (`DO $$ BEGIN ... END $$;`). PostgreSQL requires `$$` (or any matching `$tag$` pair) as the delimiter for anonymous code blocks; a bare single `$` is not a valid quote delimiter.

### Changes
- **Modified** `backend/prisma/migrations/20260314220000_sync_schema_to_latest/migration.sql`

body:
## Purpose

Remove dead code in the "tool call closing" branch of 4 streaming tool parsers.
The removed lines (`diff = diff.encode("utf-8").decode("unicode_escape") if diff is str else diff`)
were dead code -- the write to `diff` is immediately overwritten
by `diff = delta_text[:end_loc] + '"}'`, so the decoded value is never used.

`diff is str` is also incorrect, it should've been `isinstance(diff, str)`.

The code was originally introduced in
[PR #10398](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/10398) (Nov 2024) where
the decoded `diff` was passed to `json.dumps()`.
[PR #10979](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/10979) (Dec 2024)
rewrote the closing-branch logic to extract `diff` from `delta_text` instead,

author: copilot
body:
All 5 tools and 8 Watcher agents shared mutable global state with no execution boundaries, resource limits, or input validation. This adds a sandbox layer so every agent operates in its own contained execution context.

### New module: `src/sandbox/`

- **`sandbox.ts`** — `sandboxExecute()` wraps every tool call with frozen knowledge snapshots, `Promise.race` timeout enforcement, and error containment. Replaces the old mutable `let knowledgeBase` global with `getFrozenKnowledge()` (deep-frozen, immutable).
- **`policy.ts`** — Per-tool `SecurityPolicy` with least-privilege defaults: input length caps (2K–200K), output caps (50K–200K), timeouts (5–15s), and knowledge-access gating. Input sanitization strips null bytes and control characters.
- **`audit-log.ts`** — Circular buffer audit trail logging execution ID, tool, timing, input summaries (values redacted), violations, and errors. Exposed via `GET /api/audit-stats`.

### Per-tool policies

| Tool | Max Input | Timeout | Knowledge Access |
|------|-----------|---------|-----------------|
| `audit_scan` | 200K | 15s | None |
| `query_codex` | 2K | 10s | 20 chunks |
| `watcher_consult` | 5K | 10s | 10 chunks |
| `defense_recommend` | 2K | 5s | None |
| `family_threat_intel` | 2K | 5s | None |

### Usage

```typescript
const result = await sandboxExecute(
  "grimoire_audit_scan",
  { sourceCode, contractName },
  (sanitizedInputs) => {
    const report = auditScan(sanitizedInputs["sourceCode"] as string);
    return formatAuditReport(report);
  },
  { transport: "stdio" },
);
// result.output, result.timedOut, result.violations, result.durationMs
```

### Additional hardening

- **Dockerfile** — Runs as non-root user `oracle`, compatible with `--read-only --cap-drop ALL`
- **x402 payment** — `NODE_ENV=production` now rejects unverified payments unless explicitly overridden, preventing accidental deployment with the MVP stub validator
- **`index.ts` / `server.ts`** — Both transports refactored to route all tool calls through `sandboxExecute()`; sandbox metadata included in HTTP responses

## Summary

The scheduler module (`src/scheduler.rs`) is the simulation engine driving all nodes and interferers — the most complex module at 290 lines of event-driven logic. It had only 6 unit tests, with several critical code paths at zero direct coverage:

- **Two-node collision recording** — the `if collided` branch in `deliver_completed_to_nodes`
- **Active interferer injection** — the entire `InterferencePoll` event handler
- **Airtime accumulation** — `record_airtime()` calls in both node and interferer paths
- **Post-delivery poll_transmit sweep** — the request-reply pattern (lines 212-220)
- **Broadcast to multiple receivers** — multi-node delivery loop
- **Capture effect routing** — `captured` flag check through the scheduler
- **Interferer-node collision** — interferer injections participating in the collision model

Adds 2 focused test helpers (`ActiveInterferer`, `ReplyNode`) and 8 new tests (7 deterministic + 1 proptest), bringing the scheduler from 6 to 14 unit tests. No existing tests modified.

### New tests

| Test | Invariant validated |
|------|-------------------|
| `two_nodes_overlapping_tx_records_collision` | Overlapping same-SF/freq TXs produce collisions, zero deliveries |
| `active_interferer_injects_and_records_airtime` | Interferer injections accumulate airtime but not `total_tx` |
| `single_tx_airtime_is_recorded` | Node TX records exact `duration_us` as airtime |
| `receive_triggers_reply_tx` | Request-reply works via post-delivery poll_transmit sweep |

   ```
body:
## Summary

L5 replaces L2/3 as the source for all inter-region connections, matching cortical biology where L5 pyramidal neurons are the primary output to other cortical areas and subcortical structures.

### Changes
- **Feedforward**: L5 -> L4 (was L2/3 -> L4) for all 7 FF connections
- **Apical**: L5 -> {L2/3, L5} (was L2/3 -> {L2/3, L5}) for all 12 apical connections
- **L5 lateral segments**: enabled by default (`n_l5_segments=4`, was 0)
- **Dimension chain**: all inter-region sizing uses `n_l5_total` (equal to `n_l23_total` in default configs)

L5 now carries confidence-weighted representations through BAC gating + lateral prediction. Two files changed, no new code — just wiring and config.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [chardet](https://pypi.org/project/chardet) from **3.0.4** to **7.4.0.post1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.4.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Performance:**

- Switched to dense zlib-compressed model format (v2): models are now
  stored as contiguous ``memoryview`` slices of a single decompressed
  blob, eliminating per-model ``struct.unpack`` overhead. Cold start
  (import + first detect) dropped from ~75ms to ~13ms with mypyc.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `354 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/354>`_)

**Accuracy:**

- Accuracy improved from 98.6% to 99.3% (2499/2517 files) through
  a combination of training and scoring improvements:

  - Eliminated train/test data overlap by content-fingerprinting test
    suite articles and excluding them from training data
    (`351 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/351>`_)
  - Added MADLAD-400 and Wikipedia as supplemental training sources to
    fill gaps left by exclusion filtering
    (`351 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/351>`_)
  - Improved non-ASCII bigram scoring: high-byte bigrams are now
    preserved during training (instead of being crushed by global
    normalization), and weighted by per-bigram IDF so encoding-specific
    byte patterns contribute proportionally to how discriminative they
    are (`352 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/352>`_)
  - Added encoding-aware substitution filtering: character substitutions
    during training now only apply for characters the target encoding
    cannot represent
  - Increased training samples from 15K to 25K per language/encoding pair
    (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)

**Bug Fixes:**

- Added dedicated structural analyzers for CP932, CP949, and
  Big5-HKSCS: these superset encodings previously shared their base
  encoding's byte-range analyzer, missing extended ranges unique to each
  superset
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `353 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/353>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.0
   ```
   -------------------

**License:**

- **0BSD license** — the project license has been changed from MIT to
  `0BSD <https://opensource.org/license/0bsd>`_, a maximally permissive
  license with no attribution requirement. All prior 7.x releases
  should also be considered 0BSD licensed as of this release.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)

**Features:**

- Added ``mime_type`` field to detection results — identifies file types
  for both binary (via magic number matching) and text content. Returned
  in all ``detect()``, ``detect_all()``, and ``UniversalDetector`` results.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `350 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/350>`_)
- New ``pipeline/magic.py`` module detects 40+ binary file formats
  including images, audio/video, archives, documents, executables, and
  fonts. ZIP-based formats (XLSX, DOCX, JAR, APK, EPUB, wheel,
  OpenDocument) are distinguished by entry filenames.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `350 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/350>`_)

**Bug Fixes:**

- Fixed incorrect equivalence between UTF-16-LE and UTF-16-BE in
  accuracy testing — these are distinct encodings with different byte
  order, not interchangeable
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)

**Performance:**

- Added 4 new modules to mypyc compilation (orchestrator, confusion,
  magic, ascii), bringing the total to 11 compiled modules
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)
- Capped statistical scoring at 16 KB — bigram models converge quickly,
  so large files no longer score the full 200 KB. Worst-case detection
  time dropped from 62ms to 26ms with no accuracy loss.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)
- Replaced ``dataclasses.replace()`` with direct ``DetectionResult``
  construction on hot paths, eliminating ~354k function calls per full
  test suite run
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)

**Build:**

- Added riscv64 to the mypyc wheel build matrix — prebuilt wheels are
  now published for RISC-V Linux alongside existing architectures
  (`Bruno Verachten <https://github.com/gounthar>`_,
  `348 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/348>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Features:**

- Added ``include_encodings`` and ``exclude_encodings`` parameters to
  :func:`~chardet.detect`, :func:`~chardet.detect_all`, and
  :class:`~chardet.UniversalDetector` — restrict or exclude specific
  encodings from the candidate set, with corresponding
  ``-i``/``--include-encodings`` and ``-x``/``--exclude-encodings``
  CLI flags
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `343 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/343>`_)
- Added ``no_match_encoding`` (default ``"cp1252"``) and
  ``empty_input_encoding`` (default ``"utf-8"``) parameters — control
  which encoding is returned when no candidate survives the pipeline or
  the input is empty, with corresponding CLI flags
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `343 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/343>`_)
- Added ``-l``/``--language`` flag to ``chardetect`` CLI — shows the
  detected language (ISO 639-1 code and English name) alongside the encoding
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `342 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/342>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.1.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Features:**

- Added PEP 263 encoding declaration detection — `` -*- coding: ... -*-``
  and `` coding=...`` declarations on lines 1–2 of Python source files are
  now recognized with confidence 0.95
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `249 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/249>`_)
- Added ``chardet.universaldetector`` backward-compatibility stub so that
  ``from chardet.universaldetector import UniversalDetector`` works with a
  deprecation warning
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `341 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/341>`_)

**Fixes:**

- Fixed false UTF-7 detection of ASCII text containing ``++`` or ``+word``
  patterns
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_,
  `332 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/332>`_,
  `335 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/335>`_)
- Fixed 0.5s startup cost on first ``detect()`` call — model norms are now
  computed during loading instead of lazily iterating 21M entries
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,

author: bryan-cox
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it:

Enables Azure Key Vault KMS encryption (etcd encryption at rest) for self-managed Azure HyperShift clusters using workload identity federation, without breaking the existing ARO HCP (managed Azure) KMS path that uses managed identities with CSI secret store volumes.

### Key Changes

**API**: Added `SelfManagedKMS` field (type `SelfManagedAzureKMS`) to `AzureKMSSpec` with a `ClientID` for the workload identity that has `Key Vault Crypto User` role on the Key Vault. CEL validation rules enforce mutual exclusivity between `kms` (managed) and `selfManagedKMS` (self-managed), and immutability once set.

**Control Plane Operator**:
- Azure KMS provider now supports both ARO HCP and self-managed paths
- ARO HCP: CSI secret store volume for managed identity (unchanged)
- Self-managed: token-minter sidecar + emptyDir cloud token volume for workload identity federation
- KMS cloud config secret sets federated identity fields (`UseWorkloadIdentityExtension`) for self-managed

**HyperShift Operator**:
- KMS config secret reconciliation branches on managed vs self-managed, returning an error when neither credential is configured
- Credential reconciliation for self-managed Azure workload identities

**CLI**:
- `create cluster azure`: Only sets `ManagedIdentity` KMS creds for managed Azure; self-managed uses `AzureKMSSpec.SelfManagedKMS`
- `create iam azure`: Creates KMS workload identity with federated credential for `kms-provider` service account

**E2E**: Updated `TestCreateClusterCustomConfig` to handle self-managed Azure KMS assertions. Added envtest coverage for CEL validation rules (mutual exclusivity, immutability).

**Documentation**: Added KMS encryption section to self-managed Azure cluster guide with Key Vault setup and workload identity federation instructions.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes [CNTRLPLANE-3070](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CNTRLPLANE-3070)

## Special notes for your reviewer:

The self-managed Azure KMS authentication pattern follows the same approach used by Cloud Controller Manager (CCM) and Azure CSI storage drivers, which already support self-managed Azure with workload identity federation.

The token-minter sidecar mints OIDC tokens for the `kms-provider` service account in `kube-system` namespace, matching the pattern used by AWS KMS.

`kms` and `selfManagedKMS` are mutually exclusive and immutable once set — switching between managed and self-managed KMS auth after cluster creation is not supported.

- [x] Subject and description added to both, commit and PR.
- [x] Relevant issues have been referenced.
- [x] This change includes docs.
- [x] This change includes unit tests.

body:
## Summary
- **database_middleware.py**: Call `validate_session()` on each request to update `last_access` timestamps, enabling idle detection for connection cleanup.
- **session_manager.py**: Add `get_last_activity_for_user()` method that returns the most recent `last_access` across all sessions for a given user.
- **connection_cleanup.py**: Introduce a second cleanup tier — users with valid sessions but no activity for >2 hours get their database engine closed, but their session passwords are kept so the engine can be seamlessly re-opened on the next request. Users with fully expired sessions still get both engine and passwords cleared (original behavior).

## Motivation
A `remember_me` session lasts 30 days, which previously kept database engines open even if the user hadn't made a request in weeks. This change closes idle engines after 2 hours of inactivity while preserving session passwords for transparent reconnection.

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify `validate_session()` is called on each authenticated request by checking `last_access` timestamps update
- [ ] Confirm idle-activity candidates (>2h no activity, valid session) have engines closed but passwords retained
- [ ] Confirm expired-session candidates have both engines and passwords cleared
- [ ] Confirm users with active research are never cleaned up regardless of idle time
- [ ] Verify seamless re-open: after idle engine closure, next request transparently re-opens the database

author: whoabuddy
body:
## Summary

Closes #241

Makes the relay self-heal during nonce storms instead of passively returning 409s and waiting for agent retries. During the 2026-03-26 storm, 9 agents created 326 NONCE_CONFLICT errors over 20 min — these changes address the root causes.

- **Inline resync+retry on `/relay`**: When a nonce conflict occurs, the relay now does `await resyncNonceDO()` + re-sponsor + re-broadcast inline (same pattern as `/settle`). Falls back to 409 only if the retry also fails.
- **Per-sender dedup window**: Short-circuits repeat requests from the same sender within the retryAfter cooldown via KV TTL. Prevents the assign→broadcast→conflict→quarantine cycle from amplifying cascades.
- **Dynamic retryAfter**: Queries NonceDO pool health to compute tiered back-off (10s/30s/60s) based on circuit breaker state instead of hardcoded 30s. Moved to `BaseEndpoint` for reuse across endpoints.
- **Cascade-aware RBF timing + alarm tuning**: RBF threshold drops from 15min → 5min (cascade) → 3min (circuit breaker open). Gap-fill limit bumps from 5 → 15 during cascades. Alarm interval drops to 20s during active cascades.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run check` passes on all commits
- [ ] Deploy to staging, simulate burst: 10 concurrent `/relay` requests from different senders
- [ ] Verify inline resync succeeds on first conflict (check logs for "Retry after inline resync succeeded")
- [ ] Verify dedup window short-circuits repeat requests (check logs for "Sender in conflict cooldown")
- [ ] Verify retryAfter varies with pool pressure (check `Retry-After` headers)
- [ ] Monitor wallet drain time after deploying — target: <5 min vs current ~hours

body:
## Summary

This PR consolidates duplicated detector weight normalization logic and refactors embedder initialization to reduce code duplication across the codebase.

## Key Changes

### Detector Weights Normalization
- **New module** `vtsearch/models/weights_compat.py`: Introduces `normalize_detector_weights()` function and `NormalizedWeights` dataclass to encapsulate the shared logic for handling both origin-based and legacy detector weight formats
- **Unified handling**: Replaces duplicated weight resolution logic in:
  - `detectors_crud.py` (import_detector_pkl)
  - `cli.py` (_score_clips_with_detector)
  - `server_detector_file` importer (_parse_detector_json)
- All three locations now call the centralized `normalize_detector_weights()` function, eliminating ~40 lines of duplicated code

### Embedder Setup Consolidation
- **New helpers in `vtsearch/media/base.py`**:
  - `extract_tensor()`: Unified tensor extraction from model outputs (handles both raw tensors and dataclass outputs from different transformers versions)
  - `embedder_load_setup()`: Common initialization ceremony (torch configuration, garbage collection, progress reporting, cache directory setup)
- **Refactored embedders**: Updated all embedder implementations to use the new helpers:
  - `image/embedder.py` (CLIP)
  - `image/embedder_siglip.py` (SigLIP)
  - `video/embedder.py` (X-CLIP)
  - `audio/embedder.py` (CLAP)
  - `audio/embedder_clap_music.py` (CLAP Music)
  - `text/embedder.py` (E5)
  - `text/embedder_bge.py` (BGE)
- Removes duplicate `_extract_tensor()` implementations from each embedder module

### Route Helpers Enhancement
- **New helpers in `vtsearch/routes/helpers.py`**:
  - `get_json_safe()`: Safe JSON parsing that returns empty dict instead of error tuple (for optional JSON bodies)
  - `get_plugin_or_404()`: Unified plugin lookup with consistent 404 error responses
- **Refactored routes** to use new helpers:
  - `datasets.py`: Extracted `_extract_importer_fields()` helper, unified importer lookup
  - `exporters.py`, `label_importers.py`, `processor_importers.py`, `trainable_models.py`: Use `get_plugin_or_404()` for consistent error handling
  - `detectors_training.py`, `sorting.py`: Use `get_json_safe()` for optional JSON bodies

### Detector Training Helpers
- **New module** `vtsearch/routes/detectors_helpers.py`: Extracted shared detector training logic
  - `validate_good_bad_split()`: Validates presence of both good and bad labeled examples
  - `train_and_threshold()`: Unified training and threshold calculation pipeline
- **Updated** `sorting.py` to use the new helpers for consistency with detector training

## Implementation Details

- The `normalize_detector_weights()` function maintains backward compatibility by:
  1. First attempting origin-based weight derivation if `good_origins` and `bad_origins` are present
  2. Falling back to legacy `weights` key if origin derivation fails or is unavailable
  3. Raising `ValueError` only when neither source provides weights
  
- The `NormalizedWeights` dataclass includes an `origin_derived` flag to track whether weights were successfully re-derived, allowing callers to conditionally preserve origin metadata

- Embedder helpers are designed to be imported lazily to avoid unnecessary dependencies in non-embedder contexts

- All refactored routes maintain identical error response formats and HTTP status codes for backward compatibility

Implementa la historia de usuario **US-13 — Colores de etiquetas con validación de contraste WCAG** ([#14](https://github.com/Code-Dojo-Labs/agent-app/issues/14)).

### `src/components/organisms/dojo-task-detail/dojo-task-detail.ts`

Screen readers (JAWS, VoiceOver) do not announce the expanded/collapsed state of the "More" dropdown button on pages like Workspace Categories. This PR fixes the issue cross-platform:

1. Mapping `accessibilityState.expanded` to `aria-expanded` in `BaseGenericPressable` (alongside existing `aria-checked` and `aria-selected` mappings)
